In a recent development, the fact of the matter is that it doesn’t take a lot of work to find a good pair of headphones these days. After decades of competition and high-tech design, the market is saturated with dozens of high-quality options at every shape, size, and price point. Whether you’re looking for a basic set of earbuds for less than $100, or would prefer to drop $300 to $500 on a pair of wireless ANC headphones with high-tech bells and whistles like support for lossless audio files, or even want to spend top-dollar on a pair of wired, audiophile-grade cans to plug into an immaculately constructed hi-fi system, you won’t be short on choices.

Over the past five years or so, there haven’t been many game-changing innovations in the audio space, but that has led to a flattening of the field that’s great if you’re looking for a bargain. Features that would have once been considered high-end, like active noise cancellation, have trickled down into budget products, and audio quality has been steadily improving among budget- and mid-tier headphones. There are benefits to buying a high-end pair, for sure, but there are more bargains than ever before.

Obviously there are hundreds, if not thousands, of headphones out there—more than even I can test. I’ve put in a lot of time, though, going over the best, the most interesting, and the most talked about headphones, to find the ones that stand out from the pack. Because even when there are a lot of good options out there, we all would rather bring home the best.

I’ve been professionally testing tech products and audio gear, especially headphones and earbuds, since 2011. When I evaluate headphones, I spend weeks and, in some cases, months using each product as my daily driver, assessing its sound, battery life, and ergonomics. I pair the headsets with phones and laptops and frequently switch between devices.

According to recent reports, my test routine included streaming an eclectic selection of tracks from Apple Music and Qobuz to evaluate each headset's ability to produce audible bass, treble, and mid-range. I also listened to podcasts, streamed videos, and played video games while evaluating each pair of headphones.

According to recent reports, to put the headphones’ noise cancellation through its paces, I wear them on the Latest York City subway to get to work, in the large open office I share with my colleagues, and on long-distance flights. I make calls, too, carefully observing if their microphones help participants hear me clearly.

Recent findings suggest that I monitor the battery performance of all wireless headphones by tracking how often I have to charge them. I want to ensure that every pick’s battery life at least matches its manufacturer’s claims.

According to recent reports, because you may wear your headphones for long stretches each day, I carefully scrutinize the size, fit, and ergonomics of every pair by using them for hours between breaks. I also evaluate the layout and reliability of their controls, whether they are buttons, touch-sensitive surfaces, or a combination of both.

With that guidance in mind, find your next favorite pair of headphones among the thoroughly tested and reviewed sets below.

In a recent development, if I had to part with all my headphones and keep just one pair, I’d choose the Technics A1000. These wireless headphones are my fresh benchmark for all-around excellence, blending an elegant yet understated design, supreme comfort, and outstanding audio performance. That includes high-fidelity sound and efficient noise cancellation on par with the industry’s best offerings.

Featuring sophisticated magnetic-fluid audio drivers, the Technics A1000 headphones impressed me with balanced, detail-rich, distortion-free sound right out of the box, faithfully reproducing everything I listened to during testing — from music and podcasts to video content. Instrumentals in my eclectic jazz selection sounded crisp and vibrant. On my favorite downtempo albums, the bass was deep, while the vocals were superbly defined and perfectly separated.

Sources indicate that the Technics companion app gave me a rich set of tools to customize the headphones’ sound and noise cancellation. Depending on the music I was listening to, I could adjust the bass and treble levels and tweak the mid-range output to my liking, using a graphic equalizer or pre-loaded presets.

In a mandatory comparison with identically-priced rivals like the Sony WH-1000XM6 and the Bose QuietComfort Ultra (2nd Gen) — a duo of products with superior button controls, longer battery life, more futureproof Bluetooth 6.0 connectivity with the ability to simultaneously link to three devices, and full Dolby Atmos audio capabilities with optional head tracking. The last point is a step above Sony’s proprietary, multidimensional 360 Reality Audio, which is more cumbersome to access.

We’ve reached a point where a pair of wireless headphones from a reputable brand with elegant design, high-quality sound (including spatial audio), stellar noise cancellation, and long battery life costs over $400. By offering some of these features for $200, the Nothing Headphone (a) over-ear cans are the biggest bang for the buck and worth the attention of value-obsessed gearheads.

According to recent reports, design- and durability-wise, the Nothing Headphone (a) makes similarly priced rivals look generic by comparison. The headphones’ rectangular ear cups with rounded corners give them the same distinctive look as pricier offerings from the same maker. These include transparent and solid-color bits that give the headset unique character. Their IP52 water- and dust-resistance rating is also remarkable, as it’s rare for over-ear headphones at any price point.

In a recent development, amazing hardware button controls that include roller and paddle keys, as well as a customizable one, are another reason I became a fan of the Nothing Headphone (a) and all other headsets from the brand. Their responsiveness and tactility are better than products that cost twice as much.

On the audio front, the headphones delivered enjoyable, slightly bass-forward sound and immersive spatial audio. The Nothing X app offered intuitive tools to customize my listening experience, and I liked the option to link the cans directly to my devices via a USB-C or a standard audio cable. The cans’ noise cancellation was also solid, if not on par with the serenity offered by more expensive competitors.

The 75-hour maximum battery life with noise cancellation alone is reason enough to put the Nothing Headphone (a) on your radar. I didn’t have to worry about recharging the headset for weeks. Turning noise cancellation off almost doubles the battery life, bringing it to a staggering 135 hours between charges.

Bose headphones and earbuds have been synonymous with noise-canceling excellence for decades, so it’s no surprise the brand’s QuietComfort Ultra (2nd Gen) over-ear cans are the first product that comes to mind if this feature is a priority. Of course, the headphones are also stylish, supremely comfortable, and deliver top-notch sound, including immersive spatial audio.

Regarding noise cancellation, I wouldn’t recommend the headphones solely for their ability to eliminate ambient noise distractions rapidly, since that’s a given in this price range. What gives the Bose product an edge over any rival in this department is the option to customize the noise cancellation by choosing from eleven levels of intensity, then saving it into a custom mode for specific activities (e.g., work, travel, commuting, etc.) that’s easy to access by long-pressing a button.

Having a quick-access mode with maxed-out noise cancellation for work and travel, another where the feature’s intensity was set below 50% for my daily subway rides, and one with full ambient awareness at the tip of my right thumb was super convenient with the Bose headphones. Plus, I could include spatial audio in my custom modes.

During months of use, the QuietComfort Ultra headphones delivered powerful, entertaining sound, customizable via their companion app. Their spatial audio capabilities are just as impressive, and I tip my hat to Bose for making proprietary Immersive Audio technology, with or without dynamic head tracking, available on any content, not just Dolby Atmos-enhanced music and videos. That noted, if audio fidelity is your top priority, you’ll likely prefer the identically priced Technics EAH-A1000 or the Sony WH-1000XM6.

It has been revealed that calls sound superb on the QC Ultra 2, as usual. I like the headphones’ control layout, with clicky buttons and a volume touch slider that doubles as a customizable key. The QuietComfort Ultra’s 30-hour battery life with noise cancellation is far from best-in-class, but ahead of the previous version and more than enough to keep you tranquil on any flight.

We live in times when most consumers think of headphones as bulky over-ear headsets, and that’s what makes the Marshall Milton ANC special. These headphones offer features and performance you’d expect from a larger set—top-notch sound customizable via an app, reliable noise cancellation, and long battery life—in a more compact, lightweight package with an on-ear fit and scratch-resistant ear cup covers better suited to on-the-go use.

It has been revealed that sound-wise, the Marshall Milton ANC impressed me with crisp, energetic sound that you can customize via a companion app. Its noise cancellation is also stellar, though the headset doesn't deliver the same level of tranquility as a top-shelf over-ear pair. The extra layer of passive noise isolation such headsets provide is instrumental. Still, the Milton ANC makes up for it with a lighter and more comfortable fit.

In a recent development, the headphones’ knob and customizable button are excellent and miles ahead of many competitors’ control layouts. So is their 80-hour maximum battery life without noise cancellation. If you like the Milton ANC’s design and controls, but want an over-ear set, I have good news. The Marshall Monitor III ANC headphones offer similar design and controls in an over-ear form factor with a slightly higher price tag.

Review: Marshall Milton ANC Wireless Headphones.

It has been revealed that the Soundcore Q31i wireless headphones by Anker are your best bet if you want to stay in two-digit price territory. Believe it or not, for under $100, you can get a reliable set with a comfy fit, solid audio performance, good noise cancellation for the price, futureproof connectivity, and price-defying battery life in a choice of three colors (black, white, and pink).

According to recent reports, acoustically, the Soundcore Q31i headphones performed better than their price tag suggests. The sound was surprisingly harmonious out of the box and customizable via the feature-packed app. While I wouldn’t ditch my expensive headphones for the Anker offering, I found its sound super enjoyable. Their support for Hi-Res audio in wired and wireless mode was a particularly nice touch that felt unthinkable at this price point.

The headphones’ noise cancellation is adequate, if far from the best in the business. I didn’t get the same silence as with more expensive products, but I had no trouble focusing at our large open office when I put the headphones on. The key feature, like the sound, is adjustable in the companion app.

Overall, the Soundcore Q31i exceeded my expectations when I put it through its paces. The lack of spatial audio is my only gripe with the headset, but at $60 on sale, it’s nowhere near a dealbreaker.

Audio-Technica’s ATH-M50x is the first option that comes to mind when someone asks me to recommend a pair of wired over-ear headphones that offer top-notch sound, commendable ergonomics, and impeccable brand cachet, all at an agreeable price. The legendary maker’s product ticks all these boxes, so whether you are looking to take a break from Bluetooth or need a reliable tool for work, or to enjoy, say, your vinyl collection, it is an excellent buy.

A consistently balanced, high-fidelity sound is among the many reasons why many audio engineers and audiophiles swear by these Audio-Technica headphones. My favorite aspect of their audio performance is its accurate and enjoyable bass depth. Countless wired and wireless headphones, especially in this price range, are heavy on bass but nowhere near as proficient in producing mid-range and highs, which is why I always keep the ATH-M50x in my rotation.

Recent findings suggest that the headphones’ retail package is as rich as their sound. It includes three cables of various lengths and a soft pouch. Due to their immense (and well-deserved) popularity among consumers, Audio-Technica ATH-M50x headphones have an excellent ecosystem of third-party cables, cases, and ear cup covers.

If what I told you about the ATH-M50x piqued your interest, but you prefer wireless headphones, I have good news. Audio-Technica offers a Bluetooth version of the cans. The Audio-Technica ATH-M20x headphones, on the other hand, are a great option for upgraders on a very tight budget.

Sources indicate that the Technics EAH-AZ100 wireless earbuds offer the same blend of acoustic excellence and onboard features as the brand’s over-ear headphones I mentioned, but in a sleeker, lighter package with an in-ear fit and a lower price tag. These qualities make the buds my top pick in their crowded product category. I’d take the Technics offering as my sole set of earbuds over any massive-name rival.

Recent findings suggest that equipped with magnetic-fluid audio drivers, the EAH-AZ100 delivered pristine, distortion-free sound across countless listening sessions. The harmony among bass, mid-range, and treble fully met my high expectations. The buds’ spatial audio output, with full Dolby Atmos support and optional head tracking, was equally impressive. Their call performance was also stellar.

It has been revealed that the earphones’ ability to tune out ambient noise matches their audio fidelity and is rightfully among the industry’s best. Thanks to passive noise isolation from their comfortable ear tips and sophisticated hardware, I had no trouble blocking out distractions when I needed to. The companion app let me choose between fully adaptive noise cancellation based on my surroundings or a desired level of noise cancellation.

Like the Technics over-ear headphones, I compared the EAH-AZ100 buds with their direct competitors: the Bose QuietComfort Ultra (2nd Gen) and the Sony WF-1000XM6. In this group of elite options, the Technics set earned my nod for offering (arguably) better Dolby Atmos-certified sound, longer battery life, and simultaneous connection to three devices. Noise cancellation is equally great across all products, though I’d give Bose an edge for offering custom settings for specific scenarios. Lastly, this might sound like nitpicking, but the EAH-AZ100’s charging case is sleeker and fits more easily in the small pocket of my jeans than its rivals’.

Bowers & Wilkins has sterling credibility among discerning audiophiles — the folks who obsess over high-fidelity stereo sound with precise separation between left and right channels and are willing to spend massive on gear that delivers it. The British audio maker’s Px8 S2 wireless headphones should top the wish list for this group of gearheads, offering a listening experience similar to its luxury speakers in a pair of over-ear headphones.

Listening to the Bowers & Wilkins Px8 S2 headphones felt like being in a private space with a hi-fi system. Their out-of-the-box stereo sound captivated me with its accurate presentation, as intended by the content’s audio engineers. Depending on the song and genre, I could hear lively vocals, crisp instrumentals, and deep bass without opening the companion app to tweak settings. By contrast, their strong noise cancellation put me in a cocoon of silence, letting me focus solely on the music.

Of course, the Bowers & Wilkins app gave me plenty of options to customize the cans’ sound and even activate an immersive spatial audio mode. However, I liked the original sound so much that I kept it as-is most of the time, whether wired or Bluetooth.

In a manner befitting their price category and brand heritage, the Bowers & Wilkins Px8 S2 deliver style and craftsmanship in spades. The headphones are made from a mix of leather, metal, and fabric, so they look and feel luxurious. Their comfort and button controls are equally impressive, fully meeting my lofty expectations after months of testing.

Review: Bowers & Wilkins Px8 S2.

Before we dig into hardware specs and features to keep on your radar, know that spending more on your next Bluetooth or wired headset will get you better audio performance across the board and more onboard features. By audio performance, I mean noise cancellation, support for immersive spatial audio, and superior call quality, among other essentials. These features require sophisticated onboard processors and multiple integrated microphones, which inevitably reflects the retail price.

Industry observers note that many budget cans support lossless audio formats, but you shouldn’t prioritize this unless you have a top-shelf Android phone that supports audiophile-grade LDAC and Qualcomm AptX codecs. Lossless audio also isn't available on Spotify, so make sure your streaming service supports it. Apple Music, Amazon Music, Tidal, and Qobuz are a few that do.

If you’re shopping on a tight budget, I suggest spending $80 to $100 for a good pair. The most feature-packed wireless noise-canceling headphones cost north of $400, so budget accordingly if you want one. You’ll find your investment well worth it when you turn on noise canceling and discover it’s like a mute button for your surroundings.

It has been revealed that due to their lack of Bluetooth chips, batteries, and additional components to control noise cancellation, spatial audio, and other features, wired headphones can treat you to better stereo sound quality than equivalently priced Bluetooth models. Their makers can use more capable, better-tuned audio drivers while keeping the price reasonable without those extra bits, so you can score a high-quality pair from a big-name brand for less than $200.

Industry observers note that on the other hand, if ultimate high-fidelity and craftsmanship are priorities for you, prepare to spend a hefty four-digit sum to get what you need. Paired with an amplifier and lossless streaming, high-end wired headphones can help you (literally) discover new tones and layers in songs and albums you’ve listened to hundreds of times before. To be clear, though, only the most dedicated audiophiles should even consider something like that.

The headphones’ audio drivers deliver sound to your ears. The materials used in their making and their tuning are more key than their size. Translation? More expensive headphones feature more sophisticated drivers, resulting in higher-quality sound with a more palpable balance between bass, treble, and mid-range.

It has been revealed that after more than a decade of headphone testing, I can confirm that cheaper models often hide their sonic deficiencies behind heavier bass. A booming low end can affect treble and mid-range production, reducing the quality of the sonic experience even if it still sounds entertaining.

Multi-dimensional spatial audio has become a standard feature on most high-end wireless headphones. By making the sound effects feel as if they come from distinct directions instead of just your left, right, and center, headphones with this lifelike functionality will make you feel like you are in the studio with the artist, part of the audience when streaming a live album, or in the onscreen action.

Better yet, the best wireless headphones with spatial audio have sophisticated onboard tech that can process standard audio into immersive multi-channel sound, including the option to add dynamic head tracking for a truly lifelike experience. As its name suggests, this feature shifts the sound source as you move your head for an even more natural listening experience.

This feature is a must for a new pair of wireless headphones in 2025—and you no longer have to pay top dollar for it. Once reserved for premium headsets, the functionality is available across the price spectrum, including under-$100 territory. It utilizes microphones and a processor integrated into the headphones to detect ambient sounds and then deliver audio that cancels those sound waves out.Noise cancellation will reduce auditory distractions during your commutes, travels, and workday. Don’t buy Bluetooth headphones that lack it, even if your budget is below $100. Naturally, spending $200 or more will give you superior noise cancellation, often resulting in near-total silence on top-shelf sets.

It has been revealed that I typically suggest wireless headphones if you’re looking for an upgrade, not only for offering cable-free convenience but also for desirable features like noise cancellation, spatial audio, and app controls for customizing those. Look for wireless headphones with Bluetooth 5.2 (or higher) on board. These are the most futureproof wireless connectivity standards. Don’t worry if your device doesn’t support them. They are backward-compatible with older Bluetooth standards.

Recent findings suggest that wired headphones deserve your attention for their rock-solid connection to hardware, which provides instantaneous sound transmission with zero latency. Measured in milliseconds, latency is the time it takes for audio to reach wireless headphones from the source—your phone, tablet, or TV, for example. It’s imperceptible in most cases.That mentioned, a zero-latency wired link can come in handy for video-editing projects, where the audio and on-screen content have to stay in perfect sync. The same goes for competitive gaming, where every millisecond counts.

It has been revealed that opting for a cable-toting set of headphones also frees you from charging, companion apps, and firmware updates. By lacking electronic components and degradable batteries, wired headsets also last longer.

Don’t settle for a wireless noise-canceling headset that can deliver less than 20 hours of battery life, as it might not be enough to get you through a super-long flight. The over- and on-ear sets I recommend here will last at least 30 hours between charges, and that’s my minimum requirement in 2026.

Sources indicate that still, since superior noise cancellation and fancy spatial audio tax the headphones’ battery, I didn’t mind charging the Sony WH-1000XM6 and Bose QuietComfort Ultra (Gen 2) to get a better experience than what their lower-priced rivals offered. The same goes for the Apple AirPods Max 2.

If you are shopping for wireless earbuds, a double-digit maximum battery life of at least 10 hours between charges from the bundled charging case is preferable, but not mandatory. Top-tier AirPods and Bose earphones can’t reach this milestone, but they are still easy to recommend for their excellence in other areas.

Except for AirPods and Beats by Dre products, which benefit from Apple’s superb hardware integration, any latest pair of wireless headphones must come with a companion app. This includes Beats products, which can play nice with Android phones just as well as they do with an iPhone. It lets you control them and keep them up to date with firmware updates.

And look for a hard-shell storage case when shopping for Bluetooth headphones. It will keep them intact when you toss them in a bag or backpack on your way to work, or stuff them into a carry-on suitcase when traveling. No need to fret if your headphones come with a soft pouch for storage, though; just keep them at the top of your bag while packing to avoid potential (if highly unlikely) damage.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review. We may earn commission if you buy from a link. Why Trust Us?

Here’s what you’ll learn when you read this story:.

Sources indicate that I clearly remember the very last time I used one of my reliable old pyrex baking dishes, and it makes me blush. I was making a chicken recipe but had forgotten to add enough liquid to the pan. In the interest of saving time, I took the hot pan out of the oven, opened a carton of chicken stock from the fridge, and tipped a little in. That’s when my pyrex baking dish shattered into three or four large glass shards, mingled with the now ruined chicken. It broke apart the moment the cold stock touched the hot glass.

Recent findings suggest that though I was shocked, I realized what my mistake was—the glass couldn’t bear the sudden temperature change. But it made me wonder: wasn’t pyrex designed specifically to hold its structural integrity under just these kinds of temperature fluctuations? When I started searching, I found that people have been complaining about their pyrex cookware exploding for years. Perhaps they just weren’t reading the instructions. Then, I stumbled across a different reason for my destroyed dinner: there’s pyrex, and then there’s PYREX.

The first experiment to use PYREX for cooking took place more than a century ago, in the kitchen of Corning Glass Works physicist Jesse T. Littleton, whose wife used a sawn-off glass battery jar to bake in the oven. It was made of borosilicate and that was the key. Used today in cookware and lab equipment such as beakers, Corning’s “Nonex” glass was invented for hot, burning-oil railway lanterns that needed to stay intact when exposed to cold weather. Calling it fire-glass, the company later named it PYREX®, a play on the word “pyro,” meaning “fire” in Greek, and “ex,” from the label that identified its earlier product.

Since then, PYREX has withstood the intense temperatures and harsh chemical onslaughts of laboratory work. It works well for temperatures of up to 425 degrees Fahrenheit in household kitchens.

Recent findings suggest that the secret to the original PYREX’s heat resilience is its borosilicate composition, a glass made of silica and boron trioxide. Glass expands when it’s hot and contracts while cooling. Heat causes its atoms to vibrate and move apart, weakening the glass. However, boron atoms don’t vibrate or separate as much as other elements, making the overall glass more stable.

Recent findings suggest that around the 1950s, Corning also began making PYREX bakeware out of tempered soda lime glass, according to Smithsonian magazine. In 1998, Corning sold its consumer product operations to Borden, later renamed World Kitchen, then Corelle Brands. Corelle continued to produce the tempered soda lime bakeware in America—this is called “pyrex,” all lowercase. These days, Corning only makes PYREX borosilicate labware products, such as beakers, for scientific use. In Europe, the brand International Cookware still makes borosilicate cookware.

In a recent development, ✅ To have a more accurate idea of what you're buying, here’s a good rule of thumb: “Pyrex” is a brand name with clear distinctions depending on how it’s written. Only cookware marked “PYREX”—all uppercase—is likely made of borosilicate glass. However, most of this is made in Europe; lowercase pyrex brand cookware made in the U.S. has been tempered soda lime for decades. It’s still possible to locate some Pyrex brand borosilicate cookware in the U.S., but it’s harder to find. If you see the label “pyrex,” it definitely means the glass is made of tempered soda lime.

Despite its deep roots in American kitchens, home cooks have been complaining about pyrex shattering in the oven or during rapid temperature changes since the early 2000s. In 2010, the nonprofit organization Consumer Reports released a warning following a yearlong investigation of pyrex shattering incidents. “When we examined 163 incidents in detail, we discovered at least 42 reports of injuries. While hundreds of millions of dishes are used safely each year, we believe the situation is serious enough that we have asked the Consumer Product Safety Commission to investigate,” according to the report.

During testing, soda lime glass shattered at lower temperatures than “more expensive” borosilicate Pyrex bakeware, the report continued. Consumer Reports found that the iconic glass bakeware produced in America today is of soda lime, while the European-made products investigators tested were borosilicate.

Sources indicate that consumers also complained that the manufacturer’s instructions were confusing. Consumer Reports found that the small print on the back of products containing the necessary precautions is “easy to miss.”.

Sources indicate that borosilicate glass can withstand up to three times as much thermal shock as soda lime silicate. “When glass bakeware does shatter, consumers report, it can break into sharp shards that go flying, raising the risks of injuries. This contrasts with claims from one of the manufacturers that its glass bakeware breaks into ‘relatively small pieces generally lacking sharp edges,’” according to the report.

Recent findings suggest that soda lime glass is made of about 60 to 75 percent silica, 12 to 18 percent soda, and 5 to 12 percent lime. Heat-treated and then rapidly cooled on its exterior, the outside of tempered soda lime glass solidifies more quickly than the center. While cooling, the inside pulls at the stiffer exterior layer, creating tension that makes the whole piece more durable. If it does break, tempered glass forms rounded, cube-shaped chunks, instead of the sharp shards of untempered soda lime glass—think about the last time you dropped a drinking glass.

Untempered soda lime glass is used for items that aren’t supposed to be heated, such as drinking glasses and windows. It isn’t safe for either the oven or the microwave oven.

Sources indicate that so look for a European provenance, or simply “borosilicate” in the description before you buy your next glass baking dish. I know I will, because I’m pretty sure I’ve only ever owned the soda lime version.

Sources indicate that chairman Rand Paul, R-Ky., speaks during a Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee business meeting on Sept. 23. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

Republican leaders have skipped a bipartisan deliberative process for recommending the next comptroller general to head the Government Accountability Office, as lawmakers prepare to consider a nomination for the post from President Donald Trump.

According to recent reports, sources mentioned Trump is planning to nominate Eric Ueland, who at the moment serves as deputy director for management at the Office of Management and Budget. The White House submitted ethics paperwork on Ueland — required for nominations — to the GAO, according to a source.

Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Chairman Rand Paul, R-Ky., on Thursday posted notice of a committee hearing Nov. 19 to examine more than a dozen presidential nominees for executive and judicial offices, including “a nominee to be Comptroller General.”.

The post identifies by name all of the nominees except the candidate for comptroller general. The post has been filled by an acting comptroller general, Orice Williams Brown, since Gene L. Dodaro completed his 15-year term at the end of last year.

Sources indicate that the move by Paul to short-circuit the convening of a legislative commission to recommend candidates infuriated top Democrats, who excoriated the chairman in a joint statement Wednesday night. A special bipartisan, bicameral legislative commission is supposed to recommend at least three candidates for comptroller general to the president, according to statute.

Sources indicate that homeland Security Committee GOP staff solicited recommendations for a comptroller general from some Democratic congressional offices Wednesday afternoon, imposing a deadline of 8 a.m. Thursday, according to Democratic aides.

The president nominates the head of the GAO, the investigative arm of Congress, with the advice and consent of the Senate.

Sources indicate that paul pushed back on the criticism Thursday, saying, “Democrats have known about this for months and months and months.” He said the last time the special commission made recommendations for the office, when Barack Obama was president, “Democrats submitted their own list, Republicans submitted their own list. So they can complain all they want but they just need to make their list and submit it.”.

In the past, however, the special commission convened, sought applications for the position, interviewed candidates and deliberated before sending recommendations to the president.

A 1980 law states that when there is a vacancy in the comptroller general position, “there is established a commission to recommend individuals to the President for appointment to the vacant office,” and that the commission must submit at least three names.

Under the statute, the commission includes the speaker, Senate majority and minority leaders, House majority and minority leaders, chairs and ranking members of the Senate Homeland Security and House Oversight and Government Reform committees, and the Senate president pro tempore.

Sources indicate that in 1981, for example, after the law took effect, the two congressional leaders, Speaker Thomas P. “Tip” O’Neill Jr., D-Mass., and Senate Majority Leader Howard H. Baker, R-Tenn., sent a letter to President Ronald Reagan saying the special commission had met and voted to recommend eight candidates to succeed Comptroller General Elmer Staats.

“The members of the Commission have taken their statutory responsibility seriously,” they wrote.

Industry observers note that reagan nominated Charles A. Bowsher, who was on the list, and he was confirmed.

Recent findings suggest that after Bowsher’s term ended in 1996, the commission eventually formed, interviewed multiple candidates, and deliberated for several months. Republicans controlled both chambers, and Bill Clinton was president. The members of the commission could not reach agreement, and as a result, the Republicans on the committee submitted their list to Clinton, and the Democrats on the panel submitted theirs.

Sources indicate that clinton also had his own list. Clinton nominated David M. Walker, who was on all three lists, and he was confirmed by the Senate more than two years after Bowsher’s departure. Walker argued Thursday against short-circuiting the commission process.

Recent findings suggest that “The position is of critical importance and the related statutory Commission process should not be circumvented," Walker mentioned. "Doing so would undercut the credibility of the person and the effectiveness of the GAO.”.

Recent findings suggest that walker resigned in March of 2008, when George W. Bush was still president. He appointed Dodaro as acting comptroller general when he left. The commission got going several months later, creating a website with application instructions and candidate questions.

Over the next two years, the commission interviewed some 20 candidates. Democrats and Republicans on the panel were unable to reach agreement, and Democrats, who had a majority on the commission, submitted their own list to Obama in 2010. Republicans followed up with their list.

“The Commission has been working in earnest on this undertaking for more than one year and has dedicated considerable time and effort to present you with highly qualified candidates for this important position,” then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi, D-Calif., and then-Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid, D-Nev., along with other Democratic leaders, wrote to Obama when they submitted the Democrats’ list.

The Democrats’ move drew a rebuke from Sen. Susan Collins, R-Maine, who was ranking member of the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee at the time.

Collins stated in a statement she was “extremely disappointed” that Democrats “abruptly ended the selection process for the next Comptroller General without a bipartisan agreement” on the recommendations. “We have had several exceptionally qualified individuals apply to be the next leader of the GAO, and it should have been possible to come up with a consensus list.”.

Obama nominated and the Senate confirmed Dodaro, who was one of four recommendations from the Democrats.

Industry News: Havila Joins European Research Project LowNoiser

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (405 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Cruiseindustrynews

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Havila Voyages has confirmed that in March, it joined the European research project “LowNoiser,” which aims to develop practical, scalable and environmentally friendly technologies for the maritime industry.
  • The organization said that, six months later, modifications are being carried out on the Havila Capella in collaboration with Kongsberg Maritime.
  • Havila stated in a press release that on October 30, the Havila Capella entered a 28-day docking period for her first five-year inspection at the Ulstein shipyard near Fosnavåg.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Havila Voyages has confirmed that in March, it joined the European research project “LowNoiser,” which aims to develop practical, scalable and environmentally friendly technologies for the maritime industry.

The organization said that, six months later, modifications are being carried out on the Havila Capella in collaboration with Kongsberg Maritime.

Havila stated in a press release that on October 30, the Havila Capella entered a 28-day docking period for her first five-year inspection at the Ulstein shipyard near Fosnavåg.

Both Azipull units will be fitted with new propeller blades, and a new, noise-reducing gearbox assembly will be installed as part of the LowNoiser project.

The latest technology is expected to significantly reduce the ship’s underwater operating noise levels.

“All these adjustments and modifications may not seem particularly groundbreaking on their own but taken together they help us steadily advance towards our goal: that future generations – just like us – will be able to live off and along the Norwegian coast,” said Bent Martini, CEO of Havila Voyages.

In addition to the LowNoiser retrofits, the Havila Capella is also being fitted with a standardized IEC shore power connection, enabling charging at more ports.

Work is also underway on the LNG system to reduce its overall complexity. Finally, the vessel will be fitted with a fresh cargo door.

“The LowNoiser project impressively demonstrates how quickly a sustainable solution can emerge from practical research, the involvement of partners from the maritime industry and a shared vision. We are proud to be part of this project, as it underlines the expertise of the Norwegian maritime cluster as a whole,” added Martini.

Havila Voyages added that it aims to operate in a climate-neutral way on the Norwegian coastal route from 2028 and to be emission-free from 2030.

According to the press release, the LowNoiser team used hydrophone measurements, taken in the spring both on the vessel itself and in its operating area, as the basis for their data.

These measurements also serve as a reference for further measurements using the same set-up, scheduled for the first quarter of 2027.

This means that the technological improvements to the propulsion system now installed can be measured directly, and the expected reduction in noise emissions can be validated.

The release stated that in future, these results could benefit the rest of the fleet and the shipping industry through scalability.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nicko Cruises has revealed that musician Tom Gaebel will be joining a cruise aboard the Vasco da Gama next fall.

From Oct 27 to Nov 4, 2027, the singer will provide musical highlights on a nine-day “Mediterranean treasures in Spain and Portugal” sailing from Mallorca to Lisbon.

Gaebel’s repertoire ranges from his own songs to the homage to Sinatra and License to Swing featuring music from the world of James Bond and other film classics.

Together with his saxophonist, he will perform at a concert evening at the ship’s Hollywood’s Show Theater.

Additionally, cruiseCLUB members have the opportunity to meet the artist in person during the club cocktail and an exclusive meet and greet event.

The nine-day cruise heads from Palma de Mallorca to Mahón on Menorca where guests can discover the original side of the Balearic island, taste regional wines and cheeses, or hike through the s’Albufera des Grau nature park.

The ship then docks in Ibiza, after which the route continues along the Spanish Mediterranean coast, calling at Alicante, Cartagena and Motril.

After a day at sea, the ship arrives in Lisbon for an overnight stay, allowing guests to explore the Portuguese capital.

In a recent development, the Vasco da Gama recently embarked on its 193-day world cruise from Hamburg. After visiting a wide range of destinations around the Atlantic, Pacific and Indian Oceans, the ship is set to return to the same port on May 5, 2027.

Trump’s ‘invasion’ asylum ban to face justices

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (561 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the border wall is seen in 2021 stretching along the U.S.-Mexico border near Columbus, N.M.
  • The Supreme Court agreed on Friday to hear a challenge to President Donald Trump’s claims that an “invasion” at the southern border can be used to deny asylum claims by refugees.
  • Industry observers note that the Trump administration had asked the justices to review a decision by the U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the border wall is seen in 2021 stretching along the U.S.-Mexico border near Columbus, N.M. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

The Supreme Court agreed on Friday to hear a challenge to President Donald Trump’s claims that an “invasion” at the southern border can be used to deny asylum claims by refugees.

Industry observers note that the Trump administration had asked the justices to review a decision by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit that held the president could not broadly deny asylum claims under federal law. The case is the latest high-profile fight over one of Trump’s signature domestic policies.

The administration argues in its petition for the justices to take the case that the president has broad authority over asylum claims, which includes shutting down the system entirely because he has decided he will not grant any.

“The proclamation thus lawfully suspends access to asylum, which is a purely discretionary benefit. The court of appeals’ insistence that aliens are entitled to file futile asylum applications elevates empty procedures over substance,” the petition says.

Trump issued the order on his first day in office, declaring an “invasion” on the southern border and using that as a reason to deny asylum claims by refugees who present themselves there. The order is still in place, preventing asylum claims at the U.S.-Mexico border while the lawsuit plays out.

In court filings asking the justices to take the case, the administration pointed to “dramatic” reductions in illegal border crossings, which freed up resources to combat human trafficking and other threats.

In Friday’s order, the justices agreed to hear arguments over the legality of Trump’s executive order as well as whether the lower-court judge could grant an order in favor of all asylum seekers rather than just the ones who brought the suit.

Immigration rights groups initially challenged the order and won a successful ruling from a federal judge in Washington. The administration later appealed to the D.C. Circuit, where it lost at a three-judge panel before it brought the case before the justices.

Sources indicate that the D.C. Circuit held that although federal law provides a president discretion in denying asylum claims, he cannot do so categorically.

Sources indicate that the ACLU and immigrant rights groups who brought the case defended the ruling in their own filing. The filing argues that Congress mandated the creation of the asylum system and the president “may not invent by fiat a latest removal system that eviscerates the protections Congress mandated by statute.”.

Last term the justices ruled in favor of a separate policy dating to the first Trump administration that allowed officials to prevent asylum claims by stopping refugees from actually reaching the U.S. border.

A ruling in favor of the refugees could allow the administration to restart that policy and still deny asylum claims.

The case granted Friday is the latest high-profile immigration policy clash on the justices’ docket this term. Earlier this year the justices agreed to hear a challenge to the administration’s policy that most immigrants facing deportation should be detained without bond.

The justices will likely hear oral arguments and decide the case granted Friday before the end of the court’s term next June.

According to recent reports, the case is Mullin v. Refugee and Immigrant Center for Education and Legal Services.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Holland America Line is returning to Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade on Nov. 26 with an Alaska-themed float.

The cruise line will be back at the parade’s 100th edition for a second consecutive year, showcasing “The Land of Glaciers, Wildlife & Wonder” float featuring kinetic design elements inspired by the destination’s glaciers, wildlife and landscapes.

Performing atop the float will be Grammy-winning rock band Blues Traveler.

“We are thrilled to return to Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade for this milestone 100th march and once again share the wonder of Alaska with millions of people across the country,” mentioned Kacy Cole, chief marketing officer for Holland America Line.

It has been revealed that “As we look ahead to 80 years of exploring Alaska, we’re proud to bring a destination that has been part of our story for decades to one of America’s most beloved holiday traditions. Blues Traveler is an iconic band with a remarkable legacy in American music, and we’re honored to have them join us as we bring Alaska to the heart of New York City.”.

The 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade will air Thursday, Nov. 26 in the U.S. on NBC and stream on Peacock from 8:30 a.m. to 12 p.m., in all time zones.

Holland America Line will mark 80 years of Alaska exploration in 2027.

Six ships will sail in the region from April through September on itineraries ranging from seven to 28 days, including the monthlong “Alaska Arctic Circle Solstice” and a new eight-day option roundtrip from Vancouver, Canada.

Guests can sail roundtrip from Seattle, Washington; roundtrip from Vancouver; or between Vancouver and Whittier (Anchorage), Alaska.

The organization is also updating its Denali Lodge, which is getting 192 new rooms as part of a $70 million renovation.

The Adora Flora City departed from Guangzhou Nansha International Cruise Home Port on Sunday, November 22, beginning a six-day, five-night commercial maiden voyage.

Recent findings suggest that adora mentioned that the departure marks a step forward in scaling up operations. At the ceremony, Olympic diving champion Guo Jingjing served as the ship’s Launch Ambassador.

Jingjing mentioned: “I am honored to serve as the Launch Ambassador and to witness this ‘national treasure’ set sail.”.

In 2027, the Adora Flora City will operate more than 50 international cruise itineraries from its homeport. In addition to five- and six-day Southeast Asian routes, the ship will introduce nearly 10 nine-day, eight-night “South Seas Charm” itineraries.

The ship will also offer several no-destination “cruise-to-nowhere” voyages.

Shi Dai, Chairman of China Tourism Group, said the group aims to set a newly introduced benchmark for sea-based holiday destinations and “Chinese service.”.

The group is implementing decisions and arrangements made by the Party Central Committee, leading to the establishment of a central state-owned enterprise cruise operations platform organization.

Dai added: “The Adora Flora City embodies the spirit of scientific innovation and craftsmanship of CSSC.

“The Adora Flora City integrates Chinese aesthetics, Lingnan culture and the comfort of a modern cruise experience. It carries people’s aspirations for a better life and reflects the firm confidence of China’s cruise industry in pursuing innovation and progress,” he said.

As the sister ship of the Adora Magic City, the Adora Flora City has undergone upgrades to its spatial design, technology and onboard cruise experience.

According to Adora, it aims to provide guests from China and abroad with a “more beautiful, more technological, and more Chinese” cultural exploration journey at sea.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rep. Lauren Boebert, R-Colo., leaves the Capitol after a vote on Wednesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

Colorado Rep. Lauren Boebert, an outspoken conservative and Second Amendment provocateur, lost her bid for a fourth term to Democrat Eileen Laubacher, a retired rear admiral in the Navy.

Laubacher was leading 48.8 percent to 47.9 percent, a margin of 3,441 votes, when The Associated Press called the race on Friday.

The red-hued 4th District, which spreads across eastern Colorado, was unexpectedly competitive this year, a sign of how deep into red turf Democrats were able to compete this year. Boebert had Donald Trump’s endorsement, but her relationship with the president has been strained at times after she began pressing for the release of files related to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

Laubacher proved to be a strong fundraiser, hauling in $13.7 million as of mid-October to Boebert’s $1.2 million.

Boebert has been one of the most visible and controversial members of the House GOP conference since she won an upset primary in the 3rd District over five-term incumbent Republican Scott Tipton in 2020.

It has been revealed that A newcomer to electoral politics, she promptly positioned herself as a disruptor on Capitol Hill, heckling former President Joe Biden during his 2022 State of the Union address and tangling with a fellow GOP firebrand, former Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene of Georgia, on the House floor.

Industry observers note that in 2023, Boebert was embroiled in an embarrassing incident in a Denver theater that was captured on surveillance video. She subsequently embarked on an apology tour.

Running for reelection the first time in the 3rd District, which is centered around Colorado’s rural Western Slope, Boebert barely won a closer-than-expected race against Democrat Adam Frisch in 2022. When Frisch announced he was trying again in 2024, Boebert switched to the 4th District, which had been considered far friendlier terrain for the GOP.

This year, Democrats won all of Colorado’s House seats, except in the 3rd District, which is held by Rep. Jeff Hurd.

Mary Ellen McIntire contributed to this report.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fred. Olsen is offering travel agents a chance to win one of ten tickets to see Oasis in Manchester next year.

Ten agents will get a full hospitality experience to see the band at Manchester’s Etihad Stadium on June 8, 2027, including food and drink in Zadies Bar, an overnight hotel stay and transfers between the hotel and the venue as part of the prize.

The winners will be hosted by Fred. Olsen Cruise Lines account managers, Dan Scott and Pam White.

“We’ve had an incredible year working with our trade partners in 2026, and we wanted to do something extra exciting over the Christmas and Latest Year period to say thank you for their continued support. And what better way than with the chance to be among the crowd at one of the most in-demand gigs of the year?” Said Geoff Ridgeon, head of sales at Fred. Olsen Cruise Lines.

To qualify, agents must make a latest booking for a Fred. Olsen cruise that sets sail between November 23, 2026, and March 31, 2027, or between October 1, 2027, and March 31, 2028.

All bookings must be made between November 23, 2026, and January 31, 2027, inclusive, and then registered via the agent’s own account with Fred. Olsen’s Travel Agent Centre online by February 5, 2027.

Sources indicate that for every eligible booking, the agent will receive one entry into the draw, plus one additional entry for bookings made via the cruise line’s F.OCAL system, and one additional entry for every “Newly introduced to Fred. Olsen” guest booking.

Qualifying agents must also have completed the first two training modules within the Fred. Olsen Academy.

Eligible cruises include a mini cruise to Belgium, festive Christmas market sailings, a Mystery Cruise and chances to seek out the Northern Lights, as well as Mediterranean sailings as part of the Balmoral’s fly-cruise program.

“We’re always looking for upcoming ways to reward agents while giving them even more reasons to talk to their customers about Fred. Olsen. We want to showcase our smaller ships to more guests who haven’t sailed with us before, so the additional entries for ‘New to Fred. Olsen’ guests make this a really exciting incentive,” added Ridgeon.

“Thank you to all our trade partners for a brilliant year, and here’s to another exciting year working together in 2027.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ambassador Cruise Line changed the itinerary of the Ambience’s current cruise due to an issue with a fuel supplier.
  • Sailing roundtrip from Tilbury, the 70,000-ton vessel is offering a 31-night cruise to the Eastern Mediterranean and the Adriatic Islands.
  • According to an patch published on the company’s social media profiles, the change came on Friday, November 20, 2026.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ambassador Cruise Line changed the itinerary of the Ambience’s current cruise due to an issue with a fuel supplier.

Sailing roundtrip from Tilbury, the 70,000-ton vessel is offering a 31-night cruise to the Eastern Mediterranean and the Adriatic Islands.

According to an patch published on the company’s social media profiles, the change came on Friday, November 20, 2026.

“Unfortunately, the Ambience has been let down by local fuel suppliers. They were booked to refuel the ship today but have not been able to deliver,” Ambassador explained. The bunker operation was scheduled to take place during the vessel’s visit to Trieste in Northern Italy.

“The Ambience has fuel for several days; however, we do not want to get close to our reserves and have investigated several options to arrange alternative fuel supplies with the minimum of disruption,” the organization continued.

As a result, the 1,578-passenger ship will skip a planned visit to Syracuse in Italy’s Sicily region, sailing instead to Katakolon, Greece, for the bunkering operation.

The organization said that the Ambience will visit the new destination on November 23, remaining docked between 8:00 AM and 6:00 PM.

The rest of the month-long itinerary, which started in the United Kingdom earlier this month, will not be impacted, Ambassador continued.

In a recent development, “We are very sorry for this disruption and for any inconvenience. Katakolon is a very interesting port with many opportunities for guests to explore,” Ambassador added.

In addition to the fresh port of call, the Ambience is scheduled to sail to destinations in Spain and Portugal before returning to its homeport in England, including Palma de Mallorca, Lisbon, and Ferrol.

The upcoming cruises onboard the ship are also scheduled to sail from the Tilbury Cruise Terminal as planned.

In service for Ambassador since the tech giant’s debut in early 2022, the Ambience recently completed its 35th year of service.

It’s glitzy yet lush, historic yet ever-evolving, a city delightfully full of contrasts, and one I will never run out of reasons to revisit.

Sources indicate that my father’s side of the family is from Puerto Rico, so I’ve been coming back to the island for years, and I love that there’s always another corner to get to know. There’s Old San Juan, with all its pastel-painted façades, galleries and shops, blue cobblestone streets, and tucked-away restaurants; Condado and Ocean Park for long, sea-salty afternoons by the ocean; and Santurce, where street murals, galleries, haute dining, and a lively bar scene bring a fresh, creative vibe to the city.

Recent findings suggest that of course, there’s no shortage of hotels in San Juan, but sometimes a vacation to the island’s capital calls for a little more room to sprawl, or a front door that opens onto a lush little neighborhood rather than a buzzy hotel lobby. The city’s best Airbnbs offer just that, along with wonderful amenities, whether it’s a private pool hidden behind swaying palms or a breezy courtyard for sipping on some local morning coffee.

Consider this your invitation to soak up the sun in Puerto Rico's capital for a few days. Read on for nine of the best Airbnbs in San Juan to consider for your next trip.

We've selected these listings based on Superhost status, ratings, amenities, location, decor, editor stays, and previous guest reviews.

Seemingly an ode to the vibrant murals and culture found in Santurce, to describe this Airbnb as “colorful” is simply an understatement. You’ll never be bored at this retro-inspired haven, what with its groovy wallpaper in nearly every room, playful lava lamps, disco ball, and hanging plants. Conveniently, it's situated right in the heart of San Juan’s food and arts district and just a few steps from Ocean Park Beach. If you do decide to stay in for the night, rinse off the sand in your designer rain shower, throw a vinyl on the record player, and cook up some local produce in the fully stocked kitchen. Thanks to the in-unit washer and dryer, you’ll likely depart with no dirty beach laundry. As for the sleeping arrangements? The space can fit up to five guests, but there’s only two bedrooms. So if you’re doubling up, the fifth guest would have to crash on the living room’s sofa bed.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Marella Cruises‘ Discovery 2 is currently undergoing enhancements in a wet dock in Málaga, Spain.

According to a recent social media revision, the 1995-built vessel is being prepared to become an adults-only vessel, in addition to undergoing routine maintenance.

The former Legend of the Seas will undergo engine work and main pool retiling, with the Glass House Pool getting a fresh coat of paint and the atrium new seating, complete with a refreshed Snack Shack.

The ship is set to welcome only adults starting in 2027 with former youth facilities transformed into four latest venues, including Marella’s first private karaoke lounge.

Amplify Karaoke will operate as a private lounge for up to seven guests, which can be booked by the hour.

Other new venues include the Lost Luggage Bureau, a speakeasy venue inspired by the Golden Age of Travel, allowing passengers to take part in two 90-minute shows that include live music, live actors, storytelling and three signature cocktails.

The Marella Discovery 2 will also introduce Red Handed, an escape room set backstage at the fictional Cabaret Rouge in the 1920s, where teams of up to six guests have 60 minutes to steal Lady Ruby Bardot’s diamond necklace before they’re caught red-handed.

Also being added is The Loft, which is described as a calm space for passengers who want to slow down, combining a library, board games, and hosted arts and crafts in a relaxed setting.

Following the enhancements in wet dock, the Marella Discovery 2 is scheduled to operate a winter season in the Canaries and Madeira, offering seven-night cruises from Santa Cruz de Tenerife and Puerto del Rosario to destinations in Spain and Portugal.

Former Washington Rep. Jim McDermott dies at 89

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (736 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that former Rep.
  • Jim McDermott, D-Wash., a fierce advocate for universal health care and outspoken war critic who served 28 years in Congress, died Thursday at the age of 89, his family announced.
  • In a roughly 50-year career in state and federal office, the salty-tongued, liberal lawmaker from Seattle won both praise and criticism for pushing an aggressive agenda focused on expanding health care to all Americans.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that former Rep. Jim McDermott, D-Wash., is seen in a vineyard near his cottage in Civrac-en-Médoc, France, on March 20, 2024. (Ariel Cohen/CQ Roll Call).

Former Rep. Jim McDermott, D-Wash., a fierce advocate for universal health care and outspoken war critic who served 28 years in Congress, died Thursday at the age of 89, his family announced.

In a roughly 50-year career in state and federal office, the salty-tongued, liberal lawmaker from Seattle won both praise and criticism for pushing an aggressive agenda focused on expanding health care to all Americans.

As the top Democrat on the House Ways and Means Health Subcommittee, McDermott defended the 2010 Affordable Care Act that expanded health insurance to millions of Americans, while critics complained it did little to control costs.

Sources indicate that “Jim was one of the first and most powerful voices fighting to fix our broken health care system in Congress,” Sen. Patty Murray, D-Wash., wrote on X. “He was passionate and fearless — and left a tremendous legacy on WA state and its people. My thoughts are with Congressman McDermott’s family and loved ones during this difficult time.”.

When McDermott confirmed his retirement from Congress in 2016, then-President Barack Obama praised him in a statement as “a much-needed voice for his most vulnerable constituents.”.

Recent findings suggest that born and raised in Illinois, McDermott came from a poor, conservative and deeply religious family. His father, a bond underwriter, and his mother, a telephone operator and homemaker, started a church in the garage of their two-bedroom home. His three siblings slept in one bedroom; his parents in the other. McDermott, the oldest child, had the couch.

He attended the conservative evangelical Wheaton College. His bend toward liberalism began during medical school at the University of Illinois, when he voted for John F. Kennedy in the 1960 presidential election. After a stint in the U.S. Navy Medical Corps from 1968-1970, McDermott won his first seat in the Washington state House in 1970 running on an anti-war platform.

It has been revealed that he continued his anti-war stances in Congress, voting against the 2002 resolution authorizing the use of military force in Iraq. In 2013, he opposed U.S. intervention in Syria and was one of only 20 House members to vote against latest sanctions on Iran.

Shortly after he retired from Congress, McDermott settled on a upcoming life for himself by moving to a small town in southwestern France, where he admired some of the public policies he had fought hard to deliver in Washington with mixed success.

According to recent reports, “I spent 16 years in the Washington state legislature trying to get single-payer health care,” he recalled in a 2024 interview with CQ Roll Call at his home about 90 minutes outside of Bourdeaux. “Then I spent nearly 30 years in Congress trying to get single-payer. Then I came to France and in three months I had single-payer. Was that mind-blowing? You bet.”.

As he said, McDermott dedicated much time in the Washington state legislature to trying to create a single-payer system. When that didn’t work out, he developed the Washington State Basic Health Program, a health coverage system for the unemployed and working poor — the first state program of its kind.

Industry observers note that then, once he got to Washington, he tried to work with then-First Lady Hillary Clinton to hatch a federal single-payer program, but that effort came to naught. He later backed the Affordable Care Act and tried to pass his own legislation in 2015 for comprehensive health care coverage.

“The only way to truly ensure that access to quality health care is a right enjoyed by every American is through a single-payer system,” he said in a statement at the time.

McDermott will also be remembered for some of the attacks he leveled against Republicans. In the most notorious incident, he was ordered to pay then-Rep. John A. Boehner of Ohio — who later became speaker — nearly $1.1 million in 2008 after releasing a recording of a 1996 cell phone call between Boehner and then-Speaker Newt Gingrich. McDermott maintained it was worth the fight, and the cost of the settlement, to protect free speech.

“Jim McDermott was as significant as it gets in Washington state politics,” Sen. Maria Cantwell, D-Wash., wrote on Facebook. “Smart, funny, and Irish, Jim McDermott will be missed.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A-Rosa has entered a strategic partnership with Columbia blue to strengthen crew management and onboard hotel services across the European river cruise fleet.

Starting at the beginning of 2027, the Columbia signature brand will take responsibility for selected hotel crew recruitment administration and operational hotel services across the A-Rosa fleet operating on the Rhine, Danube, Rhône and Seine rivers.

The collaboration is designed to strengthen operational stability, broaden access to qualified personnel and support the long-term growth ambitions of A-Rosa, according to a press release.

Sources indicate that rolf-Dieter Maltzahn, CEO of A-Rosa, said: “With Columbia blue, we are combining the brand and product expertise of A-Rosa with international recruitment and hospitality expertise. In this way, we are strengthening the continuous ability to offer our future guests the quality and personal travel experience that A-Rosa stands for.”.

Under the agreement, A-Rosa will retain its vertically integrated business model, including its own tour operator, shipping firm and fleet, maintaining full responsibility for strategic direction, brand positioning, product development, quality standards and the guest experience.

Columbia blue will complement this by providing specialist operational services, with A-Rosa remaining the framework for all onboard hotel operations.

Sources indicate that “A-Rosa has a strong brand, a distinct product promise and extensive experience in the European river cruise market. We look forward to contributing our expertise and working together to develop an efficient and resilient model for hotel services,’’ noted Norman Schmiedl, CEO of Columbia blue.

The agreement comes as the increase in capacity, new market entrants and intensifying competition for experienced hospitality professionals across the European river cruise sector place greater demands on operators to secure skilled personnel.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Windstar Cruises completed its third Mystery Cruise, an eight-night journey along Spain’s coast aboard the Star Legend.

Sailing from Barcelona to Málaga November 4–12, 2026, the voyage took travelers to a series of surprise destinations, giving them clues for each destination approximately 36 hours before arrival.

Beginning in Barcelona and concluding in Málaga, the eight-night sailing called at six ports: Mahón, Menorca; Castellón; Cartagena; Gibraltar; Motril; and Puerto Banús.

Windstar visited Castellón and Puerto Banús for the first time and returned to Motril after 18 years, having last called there in 2008.

“Our Mystery Cruises capture what Windstar is all about – a spirit of discovery, a sense of adventure, and the opportunity to experience the world in unexpected ways,” noted Chris Prelog, president of Windstar Cruises.

“There’s something special about stepping aboard without knowing exactly where the journey will take you and trusting that incredible experiences await. The enthusiasm we’ve seen for these sailings has been remarkable, and we’re excited to continue bringing this unique concept to newly introduced destinations around the world.”.

Throughout the voyage, guests had the opportunity to experience the destinations through shore excursions showcasing the region’s history, culture and gastronomy.

Experiences ranged from coastal hiking adventures and explorations of historic fortresses to visits to local wineries, villages and regional culinary experiences.

As previously reported by Cruise Industry News, two additional Mystery Cruises are planned for 2027: the Northern Europe Mystery Cruise aboard the Star Pride and the Japan Mystery Cruises aboard the Star Seeker.

#157195. Industry News: Trump administration ups ante on aviation funds after ground stop

Industry News: Trump administration ups ante on aviation funds after ground stop

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (785 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that transportation Secretary Sean Duffy leaves a House Republican Conference meeting in the Capitol on July 21.
  • Top administration officials doubled down on calls for Congress to supply additional funds for an ongoing air traffic modernization effort after they said old equipment contributed to the need for a nationwide ground stop of flights on Friday.
  • Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin increased their ask to $50 billion on Friday night, a day after Duffy and White House budget chief Russ Vought formally requested $30.1 billion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that transportation Secretary Sean Duffy leaves a House Republican Conference meeting in the Capitol on July 21. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

Top administration officials doubled down on calls for Congress to supply additional funds for an ongoing air traffic modernization effort after they said old equipment contributed to the need for a nationwide ground stop of flights on Friday.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin increased their ask to $50 billion on Friday night, a day after Duffy and White House budget chief Russ Vought formally requested $30.1 billion.

The increased allotment, which the administration officials didn’t fully flesh out, comes after the nation’s air traffic control system experienced “instability” in its radar and communications at certain facilities earlier in the day, Duffy told reporters.

He said “inconsistency in the data” being issued by those systems led to implementation of the nationwide ground stop, saying the order was given out of “an abundance of caution” before being lifted about four hours later.

During a Friday night White House briefing, Duffy and Mullin explained the problems were driven by “an incredibly old air traffic control system.”.

It has been revealed that earlier in the day, the stoppage had caused mass confusion and raised questions about potential terror attacks, or artificial intelligence breakouts resulting from new software the agency is rolling out. While Mullin noted “we’re not ruling out anything,” he explained that “the public was never at danger through this process.”.

Still, Duffy called the incident “an emergency” while calling for additional modernization funds.

“This is an emergency,” he mentioned. “I want $50 billion. President Trump is a builder. He’s going to build this network and deliver for the American people. But the president can’t deliver for America unless the Congress delivers the money to make it happen.”.

The latest figure is $19.1 billion higher than the figure Duffy and Office of Management and Budget Director Russ Vought called on congressional appropriators to approve in a Thursday letter.

Mullin stated the new $50 billion figure was an administration estimate for a “complete overhaul of the system” which has been going through a “patchwork” upgrade process that may have overwhelmed the older equipment still being used.

“We need someone to come in and build the whole system," Mullin said. "Nickel and diming it together does not work.".

Thursday’s call for $30.1 billion echoes a White House-backed bill that Sen. Eric Schmitt, R-Mo., introduced in September, which would provide $10.1 billion for air traffic control upgrades, including $2 billion for "cloud computing and national airspace system telecommunications.".

Those funds would come after $12.5 billion allocated to the effort through the July 2025 reconciliation law that Duffy and Vought called a “down-payment.".

Industry observers note that senate Commerce, Science and Transportation Committee Republicans touted those already-appropriated funds in a social media post. They pointed to $1.9 billion provided in the reconciliation law that would go toward upgrading air route traffic control centers, which guide planes across long distances after departure and which the FAA had cited as the cause of the problem.

Sources indicate that the 22 air route traffic control centers across the country guide aircraft using instrument-dependent flight prepares. Under such plans, pilots use instruments, electronic navigation and air traffic control assistance to guide them and maintain separation from other aircraft in certain airspaces.

According to recent reports, the committee’s majority said Friday's outage highlighted the need to prioritize modernization of the air route traffic control centers, arguing that President Lyndon B. Johnson was in office the last time a new one was built.

Commerce ranking member Maria Cantwell, D-Wash., remarked in a statement Friday night that the panel is looking into FAA and airspace telecommunications issues.

“Technology complications related to how planes communicate through primary frequencies, backup frequencies, and other issues will be something the Commerce Committee will be reviewing,” Cantwell said.

Cantwell is poised to take the committee's gavel come January as Democrats assume the majority in the Senate.

In a joint statement Friday night, House Transportation and Infrastructure Chairman Sam Graves, R-Mo., and ranking member Rick Larsen, D-Wash., called the communication failures “concerning” and said their committee would “thoroughly review the issues that led to this nationwide ground stop.”.

Both committees have also been in monthslong negotiations over dueling aviation safety bills responding to the January 2025 midair collision near Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport that killed 67 people.

Industry observers note that at concern in those negotiations is which location transmission technology should be mandated to aid in air traffic control operations and allow aircraft to maintain appropriate distance. Leaders have said they hope to reach a deal in the lame-duck session.

#157194. Latest Update: How I Got My Visa to France
