    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that JSX has acquired bankrupt Upcoming Pacific Airlines, securing a regulatory pathway to operate aircraft with more than 30 passenger seats.
    • Rather than introducing latest aircraft, JSX intends to transfer existing Embraer ERJ145-LRs into the acquired airline, increasing seating capacity from 30 to 42 passengers.
    • JSX reportedly acquired New Pacific for approximately $3.1 million in consideration.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that JSX has acquired bankrupt Upcoming Pacific Airlines, securing a regulatory pathway to operate aircraft with more than 30 passenger seats. The airline, which abandoned its ambitious Boeing 757 operation in November 2025, was acquired in August 2026, although the deal only became public following a November 20 Department of Transportation (DOT) filing, as reported by AeroTime.

    Rather than introducing latest aircraft, JSX intends to transfer existing Embraer ERJ145-LRs into the acquired airline, increasing seating capacity from 30 to 42 passengers. The acquisition also creates opportunities beyond its immediate plans, potentially including higher-capacity turboprops, while providing greater flexibility amid ongoing regulatory scrutiny of JSX's operating model.

    JSX reportedly acquired New Pacific for approximately $3.1 million in consideration. According to the November 20 DOT filing, the airline intends to restart operations under the JSX Air brand using two ERJ145-LRs leased from sister tech giant Delux Public Charter, increasing to six aircraft by the fifth month. Projections include 10,106 flights and approximately 309,000 passenger boardings during the first year.

    The key acquisition is New Pacific's FAA Part 121 operating certificate. JSX presently flies under Part 135, selling individual seats through the Part 380 public charter framework. This limits its aircraft to 30 passenger seats, even though its Embraer jets were originally designed to carry more. New Pacific's certificate provides a pathway to operate 42-seat aircraft, subject to regulatory approvals.

    The move also offers regulatory flexibility. AP New previously reported how the FAA has proposed tightening oversight of public charter operators, following criticism from major airlines and pilot unions. Although those changes remain unresolved, a Part 121 operation could provide JSX with an alternative growth platform. Responding to questions about the acquisition, the company told View From The Wing:.

    "JSX is continually evaluating opportunities to support its long-term growth and bring its distinctive flying experience to more customers and more communities. As part of that work, we are pursuing additional pathways that could provide even more ways to deliver our award-winning service in the future.".

    According to recent reports, originally known as Northern Pacific Airways, the airline planned to connect North America with Japan and South Korea through Anchorage, using Boeing 757-200 aircraft. Inspired by Icelandair's connecting-hub model, the strategy unraveled following Russian airspace restrictions in 2022. The carrier lacked the ETOPS approval required for alternative routings, forcing management to seek other markets.

    Sources indicate that in July 2023, the airline instead debuted domestic flights between Ontario, California, and Las Vegas, subsequently adding Reno and Nashville. Rebranded Latest Pacific Airlines in September 2023, it abandoned scheduled operations in April 2024 to focus on charter flights. Management then pursued corporate and sports-team charters, converting its Boeing 757s from 181 seats to just 78 premium seats.

    US–Asia flights via Anchorage proposed.

    Russian airspace restrictions disrupt looks.

    Contract covering six NHL teams.

    Flying ends; approximately 115 employees laid off.

    Parent organization files Chapter 11.

    However, neither business model proved sustainable. According to January 2026 bankruptcy documents, the wider group burned approximately $5 million monthly during its earlier difficulties, while the NHL contract initially lost money on every flight. Expensive Boeing 757 maintenance and disputed payments worsened liquidity problems. Operations ceased in November last year, and the airline's Part 121 certificate became an notable asset in bankruptcy proceedings.

    JSX's immediate intends involve six 42-seat ERJ145s, where it can increase capacity per aircraft by 40% over the current 30-seat layout. Paxex.aero reports that proposed routes would average 230–345 miles (370–556 km), with approximately six daily sectors per aircraft. Higher capacity could improve economics, although retaining JSX's spacious cabin, right now featuring individual seats and side tables on some aircraft, may become challenging.

    The acquisition could also benefit JSX's turboprop strategy. The airline introduced ATR 42-600 flights in December 2025 with 30 premium seats per aircraft, and has outlined intends for up to 25 ATR aircraft, potentially including the larger ATR 72-600. Under Part 121, both types could theoretically accommodate substantially more passengers, provided Fresh Pacific secures the necessary aircraft-specific operating approvals.

    Only the 42-seat ERJ145 configuration has been revealed. Higher-capacity ATR operations remain hypothetical.

    Industry observers note that ultimately, JSX could develop two complementary offerings: its established 30-seat premium service and higher-capacity flights under Part 121. Its expanding ATR operation already demonstrates a willingness to diversify aircraft types, while Upcoming Pacific's certificate offers flexibility to accommodate further growth. The acquisition therefore gives JSX more than additional seats: it provides an alternative regulatory platform without requiring the airline to abandon its existing business model.

    FCC pick advanced by Senate Commerce after Democratic boycott

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (900 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Ted Cruz, R-Texas, talks with reporters after the Senate luncheons in the Capitol on Tuesday.
    • The fight over partisan balance on the Federal Communications Commission snarled a Senate markup Wednesday morning as Republicans advanced a controversial nomination despite a Democratic boycott in an attempt to deny a quorum.
    • Republicans on the Commerce Committee voted unanimously to advance the nomination of Danielle Thumann Severs, a senior counsel to FCC Chairman Brendan Carr, to be a member of the commission, alongside several transportation and communications bills.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, talks with reporters after the Senate luncheons in the Capitol on Tuesday. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    The fight over partisan balance on the Federal Communications Commission snarled a Senate markup Wednesday morning as Republicans advanced a controversial nomination despite a Democratic boycott in an attempt to deny a quorum.

    Republicans on the Commerce Committee voted unanimously to advance the nomination of Danielle Thumann Severs, a senior counsel to FCC Chairman Brendan Carr, to be a member of the commission, alongside several transportation and communications bills.

    The fate of the nominations and bills could ultimately be decided via a challenge on the Senate floor, according to a Democratic committee staffer, speaking on condition of anonymity.

    In a statement Wednesday morning, committee Democrats, led by ranking member  Maria Cantwell of Washington, said they objected to Thumann Severs’ nomination without a Democratic “pair” nomination and referenced a letter they sent to Chairman Ted Cruz, R-Texas, on Monday requesting the nomination be removed from the agenda.

    According to recent reports, “Commissioner Anna Gomez could be re-nominated with all swiftness, as we have called for numerous times,” the group wrote. “This is not a problem we created, but a problem that the White House can solve.”.

    Thumann Severs, if confirmed, would give the FCC three Republican members and one Democrat, Gomez. The three Republicans could then constitute a quorum on the commission, allowing President Donald Trump to potentially fire Gomez. The commission generally has five members, three of the president’s party and two in the minority.

    Cruz stated at the markup that there is nothing in the law that requires moving nominees in pairs, and that committee Republicans would continue their work on what he called a nomination that followed a “typical process.”.

    Recent findings suggest that “Democrats will control the Senate, unfortunately, in January,” Cruz noted. “But today is November 18th. The American people elected each of us to fulfill our duties, including advice and consent, for our full terms.”.

    Related: Threats to broadcasters hang over FCC nominee hearing.

    The Democratic staffer told reporters that because the committee did not adopt rules at the beginning of the 119th Congress, it has been operating under rules from the 118th, which required the attendance of at least one member of the minority party to constitute a quorum for reporting bills or nominations.

    Sources indicate that “The remaining recourse is to basically go to the floor and . . . make an inquiry in terms of what took place today, and then there would have to be a formal ruling by the chair,” they said.

    They added that in determining whether the committee had a quorum to advance the nomination, “It would depend on how they view our committee rules from the 118th that we practice under for the 119th versus what the Senate rules are.” The staffer said they have not yet spoken with committee Democrats or Democratic leadership about plans for such an inquiry.

    According to recent reports, democrats also previously boycotted a committee markup in March over an aviation safety bill left off the committee’s agenda, after which action was deferred. The committee later came to agreement and rescheduled the markup.

    In their letter Monday, Democrats quoted Cruz from a 2014 statement about the nomination of Loretta Lynch to be attorney general.

    “As you wrote in 2014, controversial nominees ‘should not be confirmed in the lame duck session of Congress by senators who just lost their seats and are no longer accountable to the voters.’ We agree,” the letter stated.

    On Tuesday, Sen. Ben Ray Luján, D-N.M., wrote his own letter to Cruz calling for the removal of the nomination from the agenda based on grounds that Thumann Severs lied to the committee.

    “While Ms. Thumann testified she did not work ‘on any media-related concerns,’ documents obtained through Freedom of Information Act requests demonstrate that she worked on several media related issues, including on commitments that Skydance made to pave the way for FCC approval of its merger with Paramount,” Luján wrote.

    Democrats have criticized the FCC and Carr for allowing media consolidation, including by Skydance. There has also been bipartisan criticism of Carr’s threats against broadcasters for speech he disagrees with.

    Luján told reporters Wednesday prior to the markup that he expects, under Democratic control next year, Carr and potentially Thumann Severs would be called to testify.

    “I have questions. I certainly hope that Brendan Carr will voluntarily show up to this committee when invited, and that other rules and tools do not need to be used,” Luján said, responding to a question about possibly subpoenaing Carr. “But . . . everything should be on the table.”.

    Industry observers note that sen. Jerry Moran, R-Kan., noted at the markup that he spoke with Thumann Severs about her role at the FCC and her “lack of engagement” as the commission has made decisions regarding broadcasters. He also said he found her testimony at last week’s nomination hearing “comforting.”.

    According to recent reports, “I have concerns with FCC action in regard to political speech, broadcasters, and she indicated in her answers . . . in a way that provided me with a level of comfort about her nomination in regard to that matter,” Moran said.

    Moran also noted he hopes to meet with Thumann Severs before her nomination is brought to the floor.

    Tech Report: Messy start to Thanksgiving travel: Delta flight cancellations spill into Monday

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (651 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thepointsguy

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that delta Air Lines flight cancellations spilled into Monday after a tech outage snarled air traffic on Sunday.
    • In a recent development, by 7:15 a.m.
    • It came after the airline canceled or delayed thousands of flights on Sunday following a problem with a key system that automates weight and balance calculations.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that delta Air Lines flight cancellations spilled into Monday after a tech outage snarled air traffic on Sunday. Combined with bad weather, it's made for a messy start to the Thanksgiving travel rush.

    In a recent development, by 7:15 a.m. EST Monday, Delta had canceled at least 92 mainline flights for the day. That's about 2% of its planned schedule.

    It came after the airline canceled or delayed thousands of flights on Sunday following a problem with a key system that automates weight and balance calculations.

    The disruption led to mass delays at its Atlanta mega-hub — the world’s busiest airport — and cascaded to other airports around the country.

    Delta said it had restored its automated system by late Sunday afternoon. But the disruptions continued to climb as the carrier worked to get operations fully back on track — and Mother Nature didn't help, either.

    Delta's operations appeared to be improving on Monday, but travelers still had to deal with some residual disruptions from a messy Sunday at airports — especially on the East Coast.

    Around 70% of the flight disruptions were due to the tech challenges, the airline had stated. The rest were tied to Sunday's weather problems, and air traffic control delays that resulted.

    “We thank our customers for their patience and our people for their professionalism," Delta mentioned in a statement to TPG.

    Travelers had other problems to contend with as the Thanksgiving rush got underway, too.

    Mother Nature also slowed air traffic at some major hubs.

    Low cloud ceilings and poor visibility fueled flight delays and led to dozens of planes getting diverted.

    Upcoming York’s LaGuardia Airport (LGA) was most heavily affected, with nearly 60% of all departing and arriving flights delayed Sunday, per FlightAware.

    42 flights headed to LGA on Sunday were diverted to other airports, according to aviation analytics firm Cirium.

    Many of those flights landed instead in Philadelphia; Albany, N.Y.; Harrisburg, PA; and Syracuse, N.Y.

    These disruptions come a week after one of the most chaotic weekends at airports in recent memory.

    In a recent development, more than 18,000 flights were canceled last weekend after an outage on Nov. 13 to critical Federal Aviation Administration technology.

    Last week, a brief technical outage at United Airlines also fueled a host of flight delays.

    Recent findings suggest that what to do if you’re affected: This week, the TPG team put our heads together to offer some of our top tips for navigating a travel meltdown. Here’s what to know.

    It has been revealed that if your flight is canceled or significantly delayed, you’re entitled to a refund under U.S. Department of Transportation policy — but only if you choose not to fly.

    If you get stranded in Sunday’s travel mess, it pays to know what the reason was for the disruption.

    Sources indicate that if you get stuck because of Delta’s tech outage, the carrier may be willing to pay for any hotel, meal and ground transportation costs you incur — if it’s a major delay. See details at FlightRights.gov.

    The carrier on Sunday acknowledged it was providing those accommodations to passengers "when necessary.".

    If you get stuck because of bad weather, it's less likely your airline will offer any sort of compensation. But keep your receipts: If you paid for your trip with a credit card that has travel insurance, you might be able to file a claim and seek reimbursement.

    These latest travel woes also coincide, of course, with the start of the Thanksgiving travel rush — with airports expected to be very busy with holiday travelers over the next few days.

    All eyes are on next Sunday — Nov. 29 — which could be the busiest day of the year to fly.

    In a recent development, last year, the Sunday after Thanksgiving set the record as the most crowded day ever at U.S. airports.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Atmos™ Rewards Visa Signature® Business Card is the business credit card of Atmos Rewards, which is the loyalty program of Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines.
    • The card has just undergone a full refresh, and there are many reasons to consider picking up this card, especially if you fly Alaska or Hawaiian with any frequency.
    • Link: Learn more about the Atmos™ Rewards Visa Signature® Business Card.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Atmos™ Rewards Visa Signature® Business Card is the business credit card of Atmos Rewards, which is the loyalty program of Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines. The card is issued by Bank of America, and is a rebranding of the former Alaska Airlines Visa Business Card.

    The card has just undergone a full refresh, and there are many reasons to consider picking up this card, especially if you fly Alaska or Hawaiian with any frequency. This post is my in-depth Atmos Rewards Business Card review, so I’d like to take a look at the card’s value proposition, for anyone who may be considering applying.

    Link: Learn more about the Atmos™ Rewards Visa Signature® Business Card.

    Before I get into my Atmos Rewards Business Card review, here’s a brief summary of the key details of the card:.

    Below are what I consider to be the pros and cons of the Atmos Rewards Business Card.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card is the only business card in the Atmos Rewards ecosystem. To start, let’s cover the welcome bonus, card eligibility rules, annual fee, and more, since these are notable factors that cardmembers consider.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card is offering a limited time welcome bonus where you’ll get 90,000 bonus points after you make $6,000 or more in purchases within the first 90 days of opening your account. This is the best publicly available bonus that we’ve ever seen on the card, and you can find the bonus offer history in this post.

    Based on my latest miles & points valuations, Atmos Rewards points are worth 1.5 cents each, given the great uses of these rewards. That means the 90,000 points are worth $1,350 for me.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card is issued by Bank of America. The good news is that eligibility for this card is unrelated to having any other Atmos Rewards card, so you’re eligible for this card (including the bonus) if you have the Atmos™ Rewards Ascent Visa Signature® credit card (learn more) or Atmos™ Rewards Summit Visa Infinite® Credit Card (learn more).

    Let me emphasize that you are eligible for this product if you have any of the previously issued personal or business HawaiianMiles Barclays cards, or any of the previously issued personal Alaska Mileage Blueprint cards.

    According to recent reports, beyond that, Bank of America doesn’t have many consistent restrictions when it comes to getting approved for business cards. While Bank of America has the 2/3/4 rule and 3/12 rules, those apply to personal cards, and not business cards. Generally those with a Bank of America banking relationship also have the best odds of approval (though it’s by no means a requirement).

    It has been revealed that there’s not a consistent credit score you need to have to be approved for this card, though personally I’d hope to have a score in the “good” to “excellent” range, ideally 700+ points. However, people with lower scores have been approved, and people with higher scores have been rejected.

    Applying for this card won’t count as a further card toward Chase’s 5/24 limit, in case that’s a limit you’re trying to stay under.

    I should also mention the following restriction in the terms:.

    I also understand that I may be declined for additional credit card accounts if my business entity currently has, or has had, another business card with Bank of America in the preceding 24 month period.

    It has been revealed that on the surface, this suggests you may be declined for a Bank of America business card if you have another Bank of America business card. However, anecdotally, this doesn’t appear to be enforced much. I think the term “may” is the key here (which is different than “will”).

    Recent findings suggest that the Atmos Rewards Business Card has a $195 annual fee. That’s on the steep side, though the card does have some premium perks. The good news is that you can add employee cards at no extra cost, so that annual fee covers the cost for all the cards you’ll have.

    Industry observers note that the Atmos Rewards Business Card has bonus categories that can help you rack up points faster. Furthermore, spending on the card can help you earn Atmos Rewards elite status. Let’s talk about how rewarding spending on the card can be.

    It has been revealed that the Atmos Rewards Business Card offers 10x points per dollar spent on flights booked through the Atmos for Business website. If you’re looking to maximize your earning, this is where you want to book your Alaska and Hawaiian flights, as this is an incredible deal.

    Industry observers note that you do need your own business to participate in the Atmos for Business program, and once registered, the return on spending is really tough to beat. Based on my valuation of points, that’s like an incremental 15% return on eligible airfare spending, on top of what you otherwise earn.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card offers 3x points on all other eligible Alaska and Hawaiian purchases, with no caps. Based on my valuation of Atmos Rewards points, that’s like a 4.5% return on spending. So if you fly either of those Alaska Air Group carriers with any frequency, that’s a solid return on that spending.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card offers 2x points on eligible dining purchases. Based on my valuation of Atmos Rewards points, that’s like a 1.5% return on spending. It’s always nice to earn bonus points, though in fairness, 2x points isn’t exactly the biggest return on spending that we’ve seen.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card offers 1x points on all other eligible spending. Based on my valuation of Atmos Rewards points, that’s like a 1.5% return on spending. As you might expect, there are more exciting cards for everyday spending, as independently, that’s not a terribly exciting return.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card can help you earn elite status in the Atmos Rewards program. Specifically, the card offers one status point for every $3 in eligible spending. There’s no cap on how many status points you can earn with the card.

    If you are serious about earning status with spending, I’d recommend instead considering the Atmos™ Rewards Summit Visa Infinite® Credit Card (learn more), which offers one status point for every $2 in eligible spending.

    Beyond the ability to earn one status point per $3 spent, the Atmos Rewards Business Card offers some additional threshold bonuses for spending, including bonus status points and discount codes:.

    Sources indicate that in other words, spending $200,000 per anniversary year would earn you 20,000 bonus status points, plus a discount code for 50% off a base fare. Just to cover the basics of that 50% off base fare discount code, here’s how that works:.

    According to recent reports, so the value of this will depend on how you’d usually travel, but this could easily save you many hundreds of dollars, depending on the type of ticket you book. It’s also still possible to upgrade these tickets, but at least the initial booking has to be in economy.

    Recent findings suggest that the Atmos Rewards Business Card also offers a Bank of America relationship bonus. If you have an eligible small business Bank of America checking or savings account, you’ll receive a bonus equal to 10% of the points you earn on each dollar spent.

    This is a way to earn even more rewards, as you’d earn 11x points on Atmos for Business purchases, 3.3x points on Alaska and Hawaiian purchases, 2.2x points on the other purchases eligible for bonus categories, and 1.1x points on everyday spending.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card has no foreign transaction fees, so it’s a decent card to use for purchases abroad, since you can rack up rewards without paying a fee.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card offers a variety of benefits and credits, which can potentially more than justify the annual fee year after year. These perks are the main reason you want to consider picking up this card, in addition to the great welcome bonus. In no particular order, let’s go over the main benefits.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card offers a free checked bag for you and up to six guests on the same reservation when flying on Alaska or Hawaiian. In order to be eligible for this perk, you need to charge the cost of the ticket to your card. Another great thing is that authorized users on the card can also receive this benefit, as long as their ticket is purchased with the card, so that’s a huge incentive to add authorized users to the card.

    It has been revealed that this is a great benefit that could save you a lot of money — Alaska and Hawaiian ordinarily charge $30-45 per checked bag, so that’s a savings of up to $90 per person roundtrip, if checking bags. If you fly Alaska or Hawaiian fairly often but don’t have elite status, that alone could promptly more than justify the annual fee.

    Sources indicate that the Atmos Rewards Business Card offers preferred boarding for you and up to six guests on the same reservation. In order to be eligible for this perk, you need to charge the cost of the ticket to your card. Another great thing is that authorized customers on the card can also receive this benefit, as long as their ticket is purchased with the card.

    In a recent development, this is a valuable benefit that helps you ensure that there’s space in the overhead bin for your bags. It’s also an awesome authorized user perk, so that you can share this benefit with others.

    Industry observers note that the Atmos Rewards Business Card offers four Alaska Lounge passes annually. The way this works, the primary cardmember will have one Alaska Lounge pass deposited into their Atmos Rewards account at the beginning of the quarter, valid through the end of the quarter.

    Sources indicate that each is valid for access to Alaska Lounges on a single calendar day, in conjunction with a same day flight operated by Alaska, Hawaiian, a oneworld airline, or an Alaska global partner. Each pass is valid for one adult, plus accompanying children. For what it’s worth, a day pass would otherwise cost $60 per person.

    It has been revealed that if you’re the primary cardmember on the Atmos Rewards Business Card, you can share your Atmos Rewards points with other members at no cost.     💡 Key Takeaways
    • Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., holds a news conference in the Capitol on Nov.
    • Saying that “Medicare for All” is no longer “a radical idea,” Sen.
    • Industry observers note that democrats could bring it about through the filibuster-proof budget reconciliation process, the Vermont independent and avowed democratic socialist told reporters.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., holds a news conference in the Capitol on Nov. 10. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

    Saying that “Medicare for All” is no longer “a radical idea,” Sen. Bernie Sanders said Wednesday that he would prioritize passing the universal health care proposal if he assumes the chairmanship of the Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee next year as expected.

    Industry observers note that democrats could bring it about through the filibuster-proof budget reconciliation process, the Vermont independent and avowed democratic socialist told reporters. And the idea could be buoyed by an influx of progressive lawmakers elected in the midterms.

    According to recent reports, sanders stated Medicare for All is gaining support from voters across the country who are looking to overhaul the American health care system as costs have soared. Democrats on the committee will move the legislation “as aggressively as we can, as rapidly as we can,” he said.

    According to recent reports, his version, introduced in April and referred to the Senate Finance Committee, would implement the universal health care system over four years. In the first year, the the age of Medicare eligibility would drop to 55 from 65, while coverage would expand to include dental, hearing and vision care. The bill would also provide coverage for eligible children during the first year.

    The age of eligibility would fall another 10 years in each of the following years until the fourth year, when coverage would be extended to all Americans.

    According to recent reports, “If there has ever been a time in the modern history of our country . . . to address the crises facing working families, this is that time,” Sanders noted, noting that Democrats will have a 56-44 majority when the 120th Congress begins in January, the largest margin for either party in 16 years.

    According to recent reports, sen. Tammy Baldwin, D-Wis., along with nine other Senate Democrats, last week offered an alternative Medicare expansion initiative, which would lower the eligibility to those ages 50 and up.

    While who will be leading Senate Democrats is still an open question — Chris Van Hollen of Maryland is challenging Charles E. Schumer of New York, who has been the top Senate Democrat since 2017 — Sanders remarked he is confident the Medicare for All bill will get to the Senate floor, “no matter who the [Senate majority] leader is.” Sanders previously expressed opposition to Schumer leading the conference.

    Asked about efforts to extend the Affordable Care Act enhanced subsidies, Sanders responded he’s “all in.” However, he added “the American people and elected officials understand the current health care system is broken.”.

    Subsidies that help enrollees pay for health care premiums on the ACA exchanges were expanded during the COVID-19 pandemic, but these enhanced credits expired at the end of last year, raising costs for many who relied on them to help defray costs.

    House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, nominated on Wednesday to be speaker next year, previously outlined broader health care priorities such as extending the ACA tax credits and reversing Medicaid cuts enacted in Republicans' reconciliation package last year. When asked Tuesday how far Democrats want to lower the Medicare eligibility age, Jeffries responded, “that’s all part of an ongoing conversation.”.

    Industry observers note that in addition to expanding Medicare coverage, Sanders reiterated his push to lower prescription drug prices. The Vermont lawmaker previously introduced legislation aimed at reducing the cost of brand name prescription drugs by linking domestic prices to international price benchmarks.

    To enact some of the agenda, Sanders may have to court Republicans.

    In a recent development, sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., said last week that he prepares to serve as the top Republican on the HELP committee next year. Sanders said Wednesday that his likely GOP counterpart “has shown an enormous amount of courage in taking on Republican leadership year after year.”.

    Sanders added that although Paul may have a different viewpoint from himself on committee issues, he looks forward to finding common ground.

    #157055. Breaking: Why Ultra-Long-Haul Flights Are Easier On An Aircraft Than Short Hops

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1388 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Simpleflying ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: Why Ultra-Long-Haul Flights Are Easier On An Aircraft Than Short Hops

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1388 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Simpleflying

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, services like Qatar Airways' flight from Doha to Auckland and Singapore Airlines' route from Singapore to New York are among the most challenging flights in the world.
    • Industry observers note that however, while these flights push planes to their technical limits, they aren't particularly physically demanding on the aircraft.
    • Recent findings suggest that the lifespan of large transport aircraft is really determined by two measurements: cycles and hours.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, services like Qatar Airways' flight from Doha to Auckland and Singapore Airlines' route from Singapore to New York are among the most challenging flights in the world. They push modern aircraft to their limits, testing their range, performance, and fuel burn like no other. There's been a noticeable increase in ultra-long-haul flights in recent years, driven by the arrival of new aircraft like the Airbus A350 and Boeing 787 Dreamliner, which are more capable and efficient than earlier widebodies.

    Industry observers note that however, while these flights push planes to their technical limits, they aren't particularly physically demanding on the aircraft. Longer flights are actually much less stressful on the airframe and the engines than operating multiple shorter services in a given day with few breaks in between. Naturally, multiple factors go into how stressed an aircraft is during a flight, and time between flights also matters.

    Recent findings suggest that the lifespan of large transport aircraft is really determined by two measurements: cycles and hours. The hours metric is as the word implies, while cycles measure the number of times an aircraft is pressurized and depressurized. This roughly corresponds to the number of flights the aircraft takes, although airliners do occasionally operate flights without fully pressurizing the cabin (these are almost always ferry flights flown when the aircraft has a pressurization issue).

    Widebody aircraft operating long-haul and ultra-long-haul flights tend to rack up hours very rapidly, while short-haul airliners rack up cycles quickly. However, while hours are one measure of an airframe's lifespan, the number of cycles/flights operated is a more important metric for determining how stressed the aircraft is overall. Operating multiple flights means the landing gear and brakes are used for multiple landings, while the fuel and hydraulic systems also wear with each flight.

    In addition, each flight involves the engines being pushed to takeoff power and, typically, the reverse thrusters being activated upon landing (this doesn't occur with every landing, but it occurs onalmost every landing). This puts strain on the engines, whereas an aircraft operating a long-haul or ultra-long-haul flight only performs one takeoff and one landing. The number of hours an aircraft flies certainly stresses the airframe, but its cycles and the number of flights it takes physically stress the plane even more.

    Hawaiian Airlines at the moment operates 19 717-200s. These planes are used exclusively to operate between the Hawaiian islands, which means that they routinely operate eight, nine, 10, or even 11 flights per day. Most of these flights last under 40 minutes, so they're not racking up hours as swiftly as a typical widebody. However, despite the short length of these routes, the Hawaiian interisland operations are considered some of the most demanding in the world.

    Recent findings suggest that the aircraft's engines are routinely pushed to takeoff power, then reverse thrust is used on the runway, and then this process is repeated multiple times per day. The engines are constantly being used and rarely have time to cool down. The landing gear and brakes are used frequently, and short turnaround times mean the plane rarely rests. What's more, the environment exposes the aircraft to salt particles in the air, raising corrosion concerns and increasing stress on the airframe.

    737-600, 737-700, 737-800, 737-900/900ER.

    737 MAX 7, 737 MAX 8, 737 MAX 9, 737 MAX 10.

    One of Hawaiian's biggest challenges was determining how these aging planes would be replaced. The engines on newer types like the A321neo and 737 MAX would not take kindly to the constant stress, while their fuel efficiency would provide little benefit. Ultimately, Alaska Air Group (which now owns the Hawaiian brand) opted to use older 737-800s from Alaska's fleet to replace the 717s, presumably scheduling extra downtime due to the aircraft's size and to allow the planes to rest more.

    According to recent reports, hour and cycle limits are mainly used for pressurized aircraft because of the stresses pressurization introduces on the airframe. While other components of the aircraft also get stressed, pressurization is one of the largest stress factors. Each time the aircraft is pressurized, the fuselage expands slightly as the high pressure air inside the cabin pushes the fuselage against the low-pressure air outside. Over time, this can fatigue the fuselage, potentially resulting in microscopic cracks.

    Regularly scheduled maintenance inspections uncover any potential fatigue cracks before they become a safety issue, but the pressurization cycle nonetheless puts significant stress on the fuselage. The pressurization cycle and these stress forces were a major factor in two mid-flight breakups of the de Havilland Comet in the 1950s, the world's first jet airliner. While it was not the first pressurized aircraft, no other airliner flew so high, and the intense forces from pressurization cycles fatigued the fuselage far faster than anticipated.

    It has been revealed that metallic fuselages are particularly susceptible to the stress forces caused by pressurization, while newer carbon-composite designs are much stronger. This has allowed manufacturers to lower cabin altitudes by using higher-pressure air, which would ordinarily require a much heavier metal fuselage due to the added strengthening needed. Meanwhile, some business jets have even lower cabin altitudes while flying higher than airliners, which is justifiable as weight and fuel burn are less of a concern in private aviation.

    According to recent reports, aircraft are designed to serve for upwards of 30 or even 35 years, so aircraft engineers design them with a specific service life in mind that covers typical usage across multiple decades. Manufacturers perform fatigue analysis to establish safe limits and inspection intervals for the aircraft, while working with regulators to determine the aircraft's lifespan. This is designed around the plane's intended mission, with widebodies and narrowbodies having vastly different hours-to-cycles ratios.

    In a recent development, in addition to the aircraft's overall lifespan, various components may have their own maintenance intervals, with engines in particular largely on their own schedules. Overall, aircraft designers set goals for the expected service life of the aircraft and its components, and then work diligently to achieve them. In addition, the original limits set for an aircraft are often increased by the manufacturer later in the type's service life, usually via an upgrade that can be retrofitted onto pre-existing examples.

    It has been revealed that the A320 was originally designed with a service limit of 60,000 flight hours or 48,000 cycles, whichever occurs first. Later on, Airbus was able to increase these limits to 120,000 hours or 60,000 cycles, whichever occurs first. The 767, meanwhile, is designed with a limit of 50,000 cycles, fewer than the A320, but more hours. In addition, some aircraft types are converted to freighters later in their lives, and these projects often come with post-conversion limits as well.

    An aircraft's age is often quoted in terms of years, but this doesn't have much of an impact on its actual remaining lifespan. While age can determine factors such as reliability and which parts need to be used, planes can easily operate for upwards of 40 years if they don't exceed their hour and cycle limits. Instead, however, planes are largely retired for economic reasons, as maintaining an old aircraft that has operated for decades is possible but rarely cheap.

    As aircraft become older, they become less reliable, and maintenance costs tend to rise. In addition, airliners require multiple types of maintenance overhauls, including what are often dubbed 'D checks', where basically the entire aircraft is taken apart, which come at a huge cost. Older aircraft also burn more fuel than newer ones, which makes it much more expensive to operate aging planes. Oftentimes, airlines will retire their oldest planes right before their next major overhaul, and then they get sent for scrapping.

    According to recent reports, because aircraft are retired for economic reasons, it's actually rare to see them near their service limitations. What's more, aging planes tend to be used less often towards the end of their lives due to their high operating costs, which further slows the pace at which the aircraft approaches its service limits. As such, some aircraft remain in service for upwards of 40 years with small cargo operators and in nations such as Iran, as well as older 737s and A320s that are nearly 40 years old, since they remain within their hour and cycle limits.

    Media in Thailand is reporting on an incident that happened early this morning (Sunday, November 22, 2026), whereby a 46-year-old American tourist died at a hotel in Bangkok’s Phra Khanong area, after an altercation with a 39-year-old Italian man, who was reportedly an MMA fighter.

    Industry observers note that according to the initial police report, the American had been arguing loudly with the hotel staff at the reception desk, for reasons that are unclear as of now. As an Italian hotel guest walked past him and attempted to enter an elevator, the American reportedly grabbed him and pulled him out.

    The confrontation escalated, and turned into a physical struggle, during which the Italian man placed the American man in a chokehold, until he lost consciousness. Hotel staff called emergency services, and while first responders performed CPR, the American couldn’t be revived. Police also found an abrasion on the victim’s forehead.

    Sources indicate that the Italian man remained at the scene, and told authorities that he had been acting in self-defense, after being attacked. Police took him into custody, and he potentially faces manslaughter charges, though the case is still being investigated.

    The hotel at which this incident happened hasn’t yet been named, but this occurred at Sukhumvit Soi 48 — there are several hotels in that area, with the biggest “brand name” property being a Ramada Plaza by Wyndham.

    I feel horribly for the family of the person who lost his life. I would have to imagine that odds are high that there were likely some substances involved here, and that this all happened after a major Saturday night out. After all, most people aren’t looking to get into a massive fight while getting their first cup of coffee in the morning (or maybe it’s just me?).

    In a recent development, but my gosh, the “victim” here sounds like he was acting absolutely horribly, arguing with hotel staff, and then picking a fight with a random person. At the same time, that also doesn’t justify the response of getting into a conflict that leads to a fatality.

    I absolutely love Thailand — the people are so friendly, the food is amazing, and the country also offers such diversity in terms of landscape, whether you want a city, a jungle, or a beach. Bangkok is probably the one exception, where you see a countless number of people moving through lobbies, elevators, etc., engaged in various forms of “business.”.

    An American man lost his life in Bangkok early on Sunday morning, after picking a fight with the wrong person.     Industry observers note that donald Trump just met with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping in China for a tripartite global summit — and nobody has any real news to report, except for Trump, so desperate for media attention that he’s giving interviews to anyone holding a hot mic and a video camera. The lack of news is not just because of a (predictable) blackout enforced by the Chinese Communist Party, but because the collective consciousness of America has shut down for the next few days. If you thought the traditional four-day Thanksgiving Day Weekend was typically slow, get ready for a one-and-a-half-week productivity dip in the economy as the video game Grand Theft Auto VI goes live across the nation. Even National Review, as sober-minded as it is, has more than a few fans of the series on its staff.

    Every periodical you might care to read — even the political or news-based ones — has brought forward its big-think “review” of the game, now available on PlayStation and Xbox. For all I know we’ll be publishing one too. But I am not a gamer — not in the modern sense of the word, although I did whip out my copy of Battletoads for the NES the other day to prove that I’ve still “got it” — and this will not be a review of GTA VI. Instead, I want to talk about time spent — and time wasted.

    According to recent reports, jeffrey Blehar is a National Review staff writer living in Chicago. He is also the co-host of National Review’s Political Beats podcast, which explores the great music of the modern era with guests from the political world happy to find something non-political to talk about.

    On “Grand Theft Auto VI and How We Spend Our Time”.

    #157050. Restored to Calder’s plan, the clouds are spinning again

    Restored to Calder’s plan, the clouds are spinning again

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1151 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Alex Padilla, D-Calif., speaks during a ceremony marking the restoration of Alexander Calder’s Mountains and Clouds sculpture in the Hart Senate Office Building atrium on Wednesday.
    • The day after Alexander Calder presented his strategy for a public art display in the Hart Building’s nine-story atrium to the Architect of the Capitol, he died.
    • Sources indicate that fifty years later, Alexander S.C.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sen. Alex Padilla, D-Calif., speaks during a ceremony marking the restoration of Alexander Calder’s Mountains and Clouds sculpture in the Hart Senate Office Building atrium on Wednesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

    The day after Alexander Calder presented his strategy for a public art display in the Hart Building’s nine-story atrium to the Architect of the Capitol, he died.

    Sources indicate that fifty years later, Alexander S.C. Rower felt a sense of awe as he stared up at his grandfather’s work, finally restored to what he had envisioned.

    In a recent development, “It’s totally phenomenal,” he noted, pointing up at the now-moving clouds as he spoke, spinning his finger around. “It’s not entertainment, but it’s trying to emulate naturalness, trying to emulate what nature would do.”.

    It was a long time coming for Rower, who remembers traveling to the Capitol in his 20s for the original dedication of the Mountains and Clouds sculpture in 1987. The mobile portion stopped rotating as Calder intended in the 1990s, and it was ultimately removed in 2014 after being deemed unsafe by the Architect of the Capitol. Millions of dollars in private philanthropy later, Calder’s clouds are spinning again.

    According to recent reports, rower was back on the Hill on Wednesday for an event celebrating the restoration, joining Architect of the Capitol Thomas Austin, Sens. Alex Padilla, D-Calif., Angus King, I-Maine, and James Lankford, R-Okla., and the project’s donors. As the speakers addressed the crowd, the clouds began to speed up slightly. Onlookers gathered on the balconies overlooking the atrium and peeked through office windows. Attendees left with tote bags emblazoned with images of Calder’s art.

    According to Rower, who leads the Calder Foundation dedicated to preserving and interpreting his grandfather’s art, the mobile is rotating on a 15-hour cycle that is “totally variable.”.

    Industry observers note that “It can go a little faster; it can go a little slower,” he said. “I told the team today that during lunchtime, I want it to speed up just a little bit because everyone’s going to lunch. There’ll be … a lot of activity passing through, and then right at 2:30, well, let’s make it go quieter.”.

    It was a labor of love for those involved, and not an inexpensive one. Jon and Kim Shirley funded the $12 million restoration. Because the pieces were so large, they were transported on an extra-wide load truck and driven at a speed of 35 miles per hour from Michigan.

    “We had to call every senator or governor that we knew on that route, which went through seven states, to get permissions,” he stated. “That was a huge thing to overcome, and it all happened over a weekend. So my wife was actually on the phone with a governor’s wife on Saturday evening. The next day, he called up his Department of Transportation and got a permit.”.

    Christian Quilici, who helped manage the project on behalf of the Shirleys and said he serves as a liaison between the foundation and Congress, said the hardest part of the project was the size of it.

    “We had to tear the wall down on C Street, which nobody really thought of in the beginning,” he stated. “Nobody got how massive this was until it showed up on their doorstep.”.

    Recent findings suggest that quilici stated he spent years educating at least 30 different senators about the quest to reunite the mobile with the stationary mountains left behind. Some of the biggest champions were seated in the front row at Wednesday’s event, including Senate Democratic Whip Richard J. Durbin. Absent was Sen. Christopher S. Murphy, D-Conn., who has been away from the Capitol while recovering from a stroke but has been a supporter of the sculpture’s restoration for years, pressing former acting Architect of the Capitol Joseph DiPietro on it at a 2024 Senate Legislative Branch Appropriations budget hearing.

    “Is there any chance that before I leave the Senate, or at least before I die, we can get the clouds back up there?” Murphy said at the time.

    Padilla read a letter on Wednesday from Murphy, whose state was Calder’s home for much of his life.

    Recent findings suggest that “This statue is actually a statement on our democracy, that we have substantial pieces of monumental art right in the middle of our most important and most iconic government buildings. To get this piece of art restored to how it was designed by the artist, well, that’s good for Connecticut. But I also like to think … it’s good for democracy too,” Murphy’s statement noted.

    The restoration was funded entirely by donations from the Shirleys, who are prominent Calder collectors, according to Rower.

    “It’s very emotional to see the work completed after 10 years of us working so hard with the Architect of the Capitol and Calder Foundation. It’s a very overpowering, overwhelming emotion,” noted Kim Shirley.

    In addition to helping fund the project, she’s a former Senate staffer who worked in Hart before Calder’s work was installed. Years after her time in the Senate was over, her husband Jon wanted to show her the sculpture, now filling the space she used to walk through every day.

    But when the two arrived, the clouds weren’t hanging from the ceiling like they were supposed to be. He called up Rower, who was a friend of his, and remarked he wanted to get them back to how Calder intended. On Wednesday, the three of them stood together in Hart, looking up.

    Technological and engineering advancements allowed for newer, lighter clouds to be built and be safe to hang from the ceiling.

    “Before it was like a bulb, it looked like a hoagie sandwich, and now it looks just really sharp, like a razor cutting through space, which was Calder’s intention,” Rower said.

    Recent findings suggest that according to Rower, it involved laser-measuring the original model of Mountains and Clouds sitting in a glass case nearby in the Hart atrium. The fresh clouds, he said, are made of carbon fiber.

    “These are giant things up in the air, and they’re just so gentle and subtle,” he said.

    Younger Hill staffers don’t know a time with clouds. But for those who have spent decades in the building, it was a special moment to see them spin, as Lankford told the crowd.

    “I can’t tell you how many tour groups that I’ve walked through this building and I pointed to this, and I mentioned it’s only half there, and would take them over to the little model that’s right over here, and say this is what it’s supposed to look like,” said the senator, a former Hill staffer himself.

    Standing under his grandfather’s sculpture, Rower found himself quoting the man responsible for it all.

    “I find that everything I do, if it is made for a particular spot, is more successful,” he said, gazing up at it.

    #157049. 5 Widebody Aircraft That Define Commercial Aviation In 2026

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1430 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Simpleflying ↗ Open Full Page

    5 Widebody Aircraft That Define Commercial Aviation In 2026

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1430 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Simpleflying

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that the Boeing 787 Dreamliner and Airbus A350 are becoming the backbone of long-haul aviation; however, they are far from the only widebody aircraft shaping the industry in 2026.
    • Industry observers note that emirates alone has 270 Boeing 777Xs on order, yet expects to operate some A380s until around 2041.
    • Industry observers note that the A380 is the only aircraft on this list no longer in production.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that the Boeing 787 Dreamliner and Airbus A350 are becoming the backbone of long-haul aviation; however, they are far from the only widebody aircraft shaping the industry in 2026. While Boeing continues to prepare its delayed 777X for entry into service, airlines are ordering more Airbus A330neos and investing heavily in aircraft that were once expected to disappear from their fleets, including the Airbus A380.

    Industry observers note that emirates alone has 270 Boeing 777Xs on order, yet expects to operate some A380s until around 2041. These five aircraft families therefore serve very different markets, from thinner nonstop routes to congested hubs where airlines need more than 500 seats per flight. Purchase prices, delivery availability, capacity, and route networks are therefore just as crucial as technology. Here are five widebody families that illustrate those decisions in 2026.

    Industry observers note that the A380 is the only aircraft on this list no longer in production. Airbus delivered the final example in 2021 as airlines increasingly favored smaller twin-engine widebodies. Its capacity and four engines make it difficult to operate profitably on thinner routes, but more attractive where airport slots are limited and demand is high. At congested hubs, airlines cannot simply add departures when demand grows.

    Sources indicate that emirates is by far the largest A380 operator, with a fleet of 116 aircraft, while British Airways, Singapore Airlines, Qantas, and several other carriers continue using the type. In spring 2026, roughly 190 A380s were in airline fleets worldwide, meaning Emirates alone accounted for well over half of the total. Many operators of the A380 have found that their existing superjumbos retain their value and replacing an A380 with a smaller jet reduces available seats unless airlines secure more slots.

    Industry observers note that its upper deck accommodates large business class cabins and an onboard lounge, while the first class showers remain a distinctive feature. Emirates has committed billions of dollars to refurbishing its existing fleet, including fitting Premium Economy cabins on the A380. In July, the airline confirmed that its wider retrofit program had reached 100 aircraft across the A380 and 777 fleets, including 47 A380s. It is also converting two-class A380s into three-class aircraft with Premium Economy.

    According to recent reports, qantas plans to begin retiring its remaining superjumbos from 2028 as its long-haul fleet expands. Emirates, in contrast, expects to operate some aircraft until around 2041, as its massive global network continues to support the A380's capacity. With no direct replacement for a 500-seat double-decker currently in production, the airline will have to balance rising maintenance costs against the value of keeping that capacity available at slot-constrained airports.

    The A330neo has attracted fewer orders than the 787 or A350, but offers a combination the newer aircraft cannot always match: relatively low acquisition costs, substantial capacity, and an established airframe. The A330-900 is powered by Rolls-Royce Trent 7000 engines and features aerodynamic improvements, including larger composite winglets. Airbus states it burns 14% less fuel per seat than the previous-generation A330.

    According to aviation consultancy Visual Approach, latest A330-900s were being delivered at prices around $120 million in late 2025, compared with more than $160 million for a Boeing 787-9 and over $170 million for an A350. These market estimates, rather than list prices, help explain its appeal on routes that do not need the performance of a more expensive aircraft. Lower ownership costs can be particularly valuable for leisure airlines and operators with seasonal demand. When an A350’s additional range goes unused, its higher purchase price can be difficult to justify.

    The Five Largest A330-900neo Operators In November 2026.

    Airbus says the A330neo shares up to 95% of its airframe spare parts by part number with the older A330ceo, reducing investments in spares, tooling, and technical training. Airlines such as Delta, TAP Air Portugal, and Condor have demonstrated the aircraft's versatility across different long-haul business models. However, the Trent 7000 has also faced durability challenges, with engine time on wing becoming a concern for operators and a factor in the aircraft’s overall economics. Moreover, seating density and flight length also influence whether its economics compare favorably with newer designs.

    It has been revealed that the aircraft's position has strengthened further through several orders in 2026. Delta ordered another 16 A330-900s in January, Scandinavian Airlines (SAS) committed to 18 in June, and leasing firm Avolon placed an order for 35 in October.

    More than 30 years after entering service, the 777 remains important for long-haul passenger and cargo operations. The 777-300ER combines high capacity with enough range for most major intercontinental routes. Emirates continues to operate the world's largest 777 fleet, and the type remains central to its Dubai-based connecting network alongside the Airbus A380. Unlike the larger superjumbo, the 777 serves markets that cannot fill 500 seats per departure while still providing premium and cargo capacity.

    In a recent development, in November 2025, Emirates ordered another 65 Boeing 777-9s, bringing its total 777X commitment to 270 aircraft. The commitment underscores the role of high-capacity twinjets in its future fleet. The 777-9 will be the world’s largest twin-engine passenger jet, combining additional capacity with more efficient engines and a upcoming composite wing. However, the program has suffered repeated delays, and Boeing's latest October 2026 revision still targets first delivery in 2027. However, German flag-carrier Lufthansa, the type's launch customer, has already been planning its summer 2027 schedule without relying on the type.

    It has been revealed that existing older 777s will therefore remain vital longer than anticipated. Emirates, for example, is refurbishing its cabins with updated business class and premium economy products, maintaining their commercial appeal while replacement aircraft are delayed. Refurbishing aircraft also postpones the expense of buying replacements.

    The A350 is becoming the flagship of airlines across Asia, Europe, and the Middle East. Its composite structure and modern engines deliver lower fuel consumption than many older widebodies. The larger A350-1000 also competes directly with the Boeing 777-300ER and upcoming 777-9. Its Rolls-Royce Trent XWB-97 engines and higher capacity make it particularly suitable for airlines replacing older large widebodies while maintaining a premium-heavy cabin.

    Lufthansa took delivery of its first A350-1000 on November 10, with a 300-seat configuration featuring its Allegris cabin. Delta Air Lines, Air Canada, and Riyadh Air have also committed to the variant. The A350 family had secured more than 1,620 orders by the end of August, according to Airbus. The delayed 777X has made the A350-1000 an available alternative, although other factors also influence fleet decisions.

    It has been revealed that the A350's capabilities are particularly visible in Qantas' Project Sunrise program. The airline is preparing 12 specially modified A350-1000ULRs to operate nonstop flights from Sydney to London, beginning in October 2027, followed by Upcoming York in 2028. They will feature just 238 seats across four classes, a particularly low density for the type. The additional fuel capacity needed for these 20-hour-plus flights means that Qantas is prioritizing range and passenger comfort over the much higher seating capacity the aircraft could otherwise offer. In November, a Project Sunrise test aircraft completed a record-breaking 24-hour, 24-minute flight from Melbourne to Toulouse.

    The 787 Dreamliner combines relatively modest capacity with the range needed to connect smaller long-haul markets. According to Boeing, the aircraft family has enabled airlines to open more than 530 previously unserved nonstop routes, including flights where a larger widebody might struggle to fill enough seats. This allows network carriers to launch services that previously required a connecting flight through another hub. It is particularly valuable when demand is spread across many destinations rather than a few trunk routes.

    Industry observers note that the 787-8 serves smaller markets, the 787-9 balances capacity and range, and the 787-10 provides more seats where its shorter range is sufficient. The largest operators include All Nippon Airways (ANA), United Airlines, American Airlines, and Qatar Airways. Its composite fuselage also allows lower cabin altitude and higher humidity than traditional aluminum aircraft. These improvements contribute to the Dreamliner’s passenger appeal.

    More than 300 nautical miles (560 km).

    More than 400 nautical miles (740 km).

    In March, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) approved higher maximum takeoff weights for the 787-9 and 787-10. According to Boeing, the upgrade gives the 787-9 approximately 10,000 lb (4,540 kg) of additional takeoff weight, allowing it to carry more payload or fly over 300 nautical miles (560 km) farther. The larger 787-10 gains around 14,000 lb (6,350 kg), potentially extending its range by more than 400 nautical miles (740 km).

    What Are The World’s Tallest & Highest Hotels? The Answer Is Tricky…

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1324 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • There’s something I really love about staying in a hotel room on a really high floor, where you’re so high up that you almost feel like you’re in an airplane.
    • The question of which hotel is the tallest and highest isn’t as straightforward as you might assume.
    • Sources indicate that generally speaking, the tallest hotel would be defined as the tallest building where a large percent of the structure is made up of the hotel.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    There’s something I really love about staying in a hotel room on a really high floor, where you’re so high up that you almost feel like you’re in an airplane. So, what are the tallest and highest hotels in the world? I want to talk about that in this post, and also discuss why the answer isn’t that straightforward.

    The question of which hotel is the tallest and highest isn’t as straightforward as you might assume. And even once we do define it, there’s the question of the extent to which the answer is actually useful. First let’s cover the distinction between the tallest hotel and the highest hotel.

    Sources indicate that generally speaking, the tallest hotel would be defined as the tallest building where a large percent of the structure is made up of the hotel. Most commonly, I see people suggest that this would include situations where at least 80% of the building is the hotel.

    This is different than the highest hotel, which would be the hotel that is highest above the ground, even if it only takes up a small percentage of a mixed-use building, where there might be apartments, residences, etc.

    In other words, a 50-story building that consists exclusively of a hotel would fall into the former category, while a 110-story building where the top 10 floors are a hotel would fall into the latter category.

    With that out of the way, let’s talk about the properties that are remarkable in these categories….

    First, let’s cover some of the world’s tallest hotels. We’ll define this as hotels where at least 80% of the building consists of the hotel facility.

    Let me of course mention one downside of very tall standalone hotels — you could end up being on a very low floor. After all, if a high-rise consists exclusively (or almost exclusively) of hotel facilities, some people will end up on very low floors. The other downside, of course, is that these hotels are necessarily huge. If you prefer boutique hotels, you won’t find any on this list.

    Presently, the tallest hotel in the world is Ciel Tower Dubai. The 1,042-room hotel opened in 2024, rises to a height of 1,227 feet (374 meters), and has 82 floors.

    To go over the list of the top five tallest hotels in the world:.

    As you can see, it’s interesting (but perhaps not surprising) that all four of the world’s tallest hotels are in Dubai.

    Industry observers note that the Conrad Shanghai, meanwhile, is located in the Shimao International Plaza, and this is the perfect example of how it’s tough to define what is technically the tallest. While the building it’s in rises to such a high height, roughly 25% of that height is the spire. So technically it’s a very tall building, but the usable space isn’t as high as you’d assume.

    If you ask me, the world’s highest hotels are much more interesting than the world’s tallest hotels. That’s because the world’s highest hotels typically take up the top floors of some gravity-defying skyscrapers, and therefore, they can also be boutique properties.

    When defining the world’s tallest hotels, there are some general challenges:.

    Because of the above, there are some minor disagreements as to which hotel wins the title, but I’ll share my take (while acknowledging that I don’t have the ability to scale buildings with a measuring tape).

    At the moment, the highest hotel is the Rosewood Guangzhou. The 251-room hotel opened in 2019, and it’s located at the top of the CTF Finance Centre Guangzhou, which reaches a height of 1,739 feet (530 meters).

    To go over the list of the top five highest hotels in the world:.

    As you can see, those last two properties are kind of hard to judge, and particularly J Hotel Shanghai is tricky, given that the property is split between different parts of the building.

    Recent findings suggest that as the inverse of the above, I should mention that the Armani Hotel Dubai is located within the Burj Khalifa, which is the world’s tallest building. However, it’s located at the very bottom of the building, so that’s hardly that useful, for these purposes, since the hotel only goes as high as 39 floors.

    According to recent reports, lastly, in the interest of being thorough, if we’re going to define a hotel as being “highest” based on the altitude above sea level, then we’d of course end up with a completely different list. Hotel Tayka del Desierto is located near the Salar de Uyuni salt flats in Bolivia. It’s at an altitude of 14,800 feet (4,500 meters), so it’s generally considered to be the highest up hotel in the world.

    I suppose depending on how we want to define “hotel,” there would probably be some simple guest houses at Everest Base Camp that go even higher, but I don’t think that’s within the spirit of what I’m trying to cover here.

    According to recent reports, if you ask me, it’s always fun to stay in a hotel room that’s really high up. There’s an key distinction between the tallest hotels and the highest hotels, though sometimes, the exact rankings are a bit blurred.

    While I’ve long been interested in this, I enjoyed researching this a bit more closely, and actually having a (sort of) definitive list. Ciel Tower Dubai is the world’s tallest hotel, while the Rosewood Guangzhou is the world’s highest hotel (unless you want to consider the 120th floor of the J Hotel Shanghai separately from the rest of the property).

    Have you stayed at any of the world’s tallest or highest hotels? Does it even hold any appeal to you?

Note that AAdvantage Business was launched in 2023, replacing the previous American Business Extra program, which no longer exists.

    According to recent reports, AAdvantage Business is the name of American Airlines’ business rewards program. This allows you to earn extra rewards in a business account, in addition to the rewards you can earn through your own AAdvantage account. Best of all, you have quite a bit of flexibility in terms of distributing the rewards. Let’s go over the details of how this works.

    Industry observers note that the AAdvantage Business program has a pretty straightforward rewards structure, as it rewards members with both Loyalty Points and AAdvantage miles. With the AAdvantage Business program, you earn the following rewards, which will post within 72 hours of an eligible flight:.

    Let me emphasize that business travelers only earn Loyalty Points through AAdvantage Business when the business is currently eligible to transfer miles, and that requires either having the Citi AAdvantage Business Card, or having at least five unique travelers who have credited flights to the AAdvantage Business account, totaling at least $5,000 in flight revenue, over the course of a year (the credit card method is obviously easier).

    Just to clarify a few additional points about AAdvantage Business rewards:.

    These rewards are all in addition to the standard rewards that AAdvantage members receive:.

There’s no reason to leave those bonus rewards on the table!

    In a recent development, in order to be eligible to participate in the AAdvantage Business program, you need to have a business in the United States or Canada with a Federal Employer Identification Number (FEIN) or Business Number. Even small businesses are eligible for this program.

    The exceptions are that travel agencies, consolidators, wholesalers, and other sellers of travel, aren’t eligible to participate in AAdvantage Business. On top of that, AAdvantage Business technically can’t be used for leisure travel.

    Sources indicate that you accrue rewards in the AAdvantage Business program without any minimums, and then you can transfer the rewards to individual members, so that they can then redeem them out of their own accounts. In order to transfer the miles in the AAdvantage Business account to an individual AAdvantage account, you need to meet one of two requirements:.

    According to recent reports, the AAdvantage Business program creates a huge incentive to get the Citi AAdvantage Business Card.     There are several potentially useful perks to this card, and on top of that, the card is offering a great welcome bonus, which is the reason that I applied for the card (and got approved), as that’s a nice incentive, beyond the value of access to the AAdvantage Business program.

    It’s worth understanding how closely this card is actually integrated into the AAdvantage Business program:.

    If you’re curious about how the AAdvantage Business program works in practice, let me share some screenshots, for those who are more visual. If you want to redeem miles, the only option is to transfer them to individual members, as you can’t redeem the miles directly out of the AAdvantage Business account.
